Lady Xie cast her eyes over the bed linens — and felt a measure of relief, though she sank down onto the edge of the bed in a heap, feeling entirely undone.
—
Xi Rongyan woke in the afternoon in her own bedchamber.
When she woke, she could hear Baozhu crying outside. Still in a daze and unable to place herself, she pushed through the throbbing in her head and lifted the bed curtain — to find Baozhu kneeling on the ground, her forehead red and swollen and bleeding.
In the room sat her mother, her father, and her eldest brother.
All of them were looking at her, their faces grave.
Xi Rongyan's mind was a blank. "What has happened?"
Lady Xie lowered her head and dabbed at her eyes. She moved to sit beside Xi Rongyan, looking at her with reddened eyes: "At midday the Emperor issued a decree. You are to enter the palace the day after tomorrow."
Xi Rongyan stared. She did not understand. She turned to her mother. "What?"
Lady Xie closed her eyes and explained everything that had passed.
Across the room, Xi Rongyan's father rose abruptly, looked at Xi Rongyan with a sigh, and said: "Things have come to this point — grief is useless. The Xuanyi Marquisate matter is finished."
He sighed again. "In the Emperor's eyes, Rongyan's virtue has already been given to him. He would not allow her to marry anyone else."
With that, he walked out.
Xi Wenli hesitated, then followed their father outside.
He wanted to counsel his father to enter the palace and appeal to the Empress Dowager. After all, with so many women in the inner palace, one who received no favor would be trapped within its walls for a lifetime.
He did not want his little sister to suffer like that.
In the corridor outside, their father frowned at Xi Wenli. "Can you not see what is happening? Given the Emperor's temperament, if he did not want Rongyan in the palace, he would never have raised the matter at all."
"Since he did raise it, do you think he cares what the Empress Dowager thinks?"
"If we refuse the Emperor in our ignorance, what will he think? That the Xi family looks down on the Emperor and wants to align only with the old great families?"
He looked at Xi Wenli sharply. "Do not speak of this again. To defy the Emperor, we would carry that mark forever. The Empress Dowager cannot protect us indefinitely. The Emperor's heart is impossible to read."
"Moreover, the decree was issued this quickly. There is no room left to maneuver."
Xi Wenli paused.
He understood that everything his father said was correct. He only feared for his little sister's future.
The Emperor's moods were unpredictable and cold. How could Rongyan ever manage him?

chapters.title: Entering the Palace
chapters.content:
Inside the room, Baozhu was on her knees weeping: "I don't know what happened to me. Running along the path I tripped over a stone and knocked my head and blacked out."
"If only I hadn't fallen, I could have gone for Madam in time."
"And none of this would have happened."
Xi Rongyan already knew that she herself was the cause of this disaster.
She leaned limply against the edge of the bed, staring at Baozhu kneeling on the ground, her mind drifting. "I was certain I was going into Qingshan Pavilion. I remember reading the sign properly. Why..."
Baozhu wiped her eyes with her sleeve. "I read it as Qingshan Pavilion too, Miss. But when I ran out and looked, it had become Qingyue Pavilion."
"I truly didn't think we had gone wrong."
"Please believe me, Miss."
With that she covered her face and wept.
Lady Xie looked at Baozhu crying on the ground, her own head aching with the turmoil. "Go and have your wound bandaged first."
When Baozhu had wiped her tears and left, Lady Xie turned again to Xi Rongyan, took her hand, and wept: "Your father did not expect the Emperor to issue the decree this quickly."
"Things are as they are now — you must enter the palace. There is no way to refuse. That would be defying the imperial will."
"We can only blame the terrible chance of going to the wrong place."
"The Emperor is the Son of Heaven. No one may go against him."
Xi Rongyan still could not make it feel real.
She opened her mouth. But not remembering anything she had done while drunk, she found there was nothing at all she could say.
After a long, long moment, her face drained of color, she looked at her mother and asked quietly: "Is there truly no other way?"
"I am somewhat afraid of the Emperor. I do not want to enter the palace."
Lady Xie drew her slight daughter into her arms, tears in her eyes: "Mother doesn't want to let you go either."
"But given what happened, there is truly no way out of it. Your person has already been seen by the Emperor."
"How could I ever have wanted this for you?"
Xi Rongyan's thoughts were still scattered and unreal.
A shaft of light fell on her from outside. She felt as though she were inside a dream.
—
For the next two days, Xi Rongyan floated through everything in a kind of weightless haze. Lady Xie selected trustworthy maidservants for her and prepared a chest of silver and jewelry for tipping and gifts inside the palace.
By the Emperor's grace, word came that Xi Rongyan would be permitted to bring two of her own maidservants with her.
Lady Xie hurried to choose those who were both steady and quick-witted.
Xi Rongyan had grown up in her hands, sheltered within the main household where there had been no strife among women. She had never seen any of that, and naturally she did not know the ways of it.
The Gu family, too, had been a household of good values — concubines were permitted only if a wife had not conceived past the age of thirty — so Lady Xie had never thought to teach her daughter those particular arts.
But the inner palace was different. With so many women, Xi Rongyan's gentle nature could not guarantee safety even if she refused to compete.
Lady Xie gave Xi Rongyan one of her own most trusted maidservants, Yuzhu, to take along.
Xi Rongyan sat holding the chest her mother had pressed into her hands, listening to her mother's careful instructions: "Once inside, be sure to cultivate the goodwill of the servants."
"Many of them may seem inconsequential, but the harm they can do in secret is beyond your ability to guard against. Tip them properly. If you run out of silver, send word home."
"And the Emperor's women — I spoke to you last night about how to deal with them."
"Your cousin Yumian is one of the imperial consorts. You two have been close since childhood — she would not harm you. Remember to keep close to her. Having each other will be a comfort."
"I hear the Emperor is currently favoring Consort Wang. Whatever you do, do not contend with her for anything. Do not show your hand — keep yourself hidden. Conceiving a child is what matters above all."
"Above all else, remember this: favor and affection are all illusions. The Emperor has so many women, and there will always be younger, more beautiful ones entering the palace. His favor never lasts long."
"Do you understand?"
Xi Rongyan sat with her head down, looking at the chest in her hands, listening to her mother's words.
She had never once imagined that one day she would enter the palace.
The image of that bloodied figure beneath the white cloth flashed through her mind, and her face turned pale.
If that day she had not taken the wrong turn — would things have turned out differently?
Lady Xie saw the blank, bewildered look on Xi Rongyan's face and felt another wave of sorrow. She drew her daughter into a tight embrace and wept again: "Tomorrow the palace procession will come. You must remember everything Mother has told you."
"In the inner palace, a woman's life is easier once she has a child. I know you will neither compete nor know how to compete — and perhaps that is good, for it will keep you out of harm's way."
"But do not let people walk all over you."
Xi Rongyan at last wrapped her arms around her mother and answered in a small, hoarse voice: "Yes."
The next morning at first light, the palace procession arrived.
The whole Xi family, dressed in their finest, stood waiting at the gate and saw Xi Rongyan into the soft palanquin stopped at the entrance.
Xi Rongyan was still in something of a daze when she climbed in. It was only when the palanquin lifted that she came back to herself in a rush of anxiety. She quickly pushed aside the curtain, and her frightened eyes found Lady Xie's reddened ones through the crowd: "Mother..."
Lady Xie pressed her handkerchief to her lips and said nothing, swallowing her tears.
As the figures who had come to see her off grew smaller and farther away, and the familiar place receded from her, Xi Rongyan felt the blur come over her eyes, and a cold trickle at her chin.
She touched it. Wet.
It was Chief Gao himself who had come to receive her. Seeing Xi Rongyan's tearful face, he walked beside the palanquin and said with a smile, as though to reassure her: "Consort Xi need not be afraid. You are different to His Majesty."
Xi Rongyan pressed her handkerchief over her face. She took Chief Gao's words as nothing more than kindness.
In the inner palace with its thousands of women, how could any of them be different?
Images of high walls and green-tiled rooftops drifted through her mind. She was frightened still.
The palanquin traveled the palace path and came to rest before Guanju Palace.
Xi Rongyan stepped out. The cold reality of the blue bricks beneath her feet rose to meet her. She looked up at the tall palace gate.
Chief Gao stood at her side and smiled: "His Majesty has specially arranged for Consort Xi to reside in Hanyuan Hall within Guanju Palace. Everything inside has been set in order. Consort Xi will henceforth take the main hall as her quarters."
Before entering the palace, her mother had told her that consorts below the rank of Noble Consort were not permitted to occupy the main hall, and had instructed her to cultivate a good relationship with the senior consort of the main hall.
She thought she had misheard, and turned to look at Chief Gao in astonishment. "How could I possibly occupy the main hall?"
Chief Gao smiled at her. "His Majesty looks after Consort Xi — this is the favor of the imperial grace."
Xi Rongyan had taken her mother's words to heart: inside the palace, keep everything low-key. She was only a Zhaoyi. If she took the main hall, people would talk — it did not accord with propriety.
She could not understand why the Emperor would give such an order. They had met only a handful of times.
Or — had she done something that day, in her drunken state?
But she could remember nothing.
She was about to raise her objection when Chief Gao was already urging her along: "Consort Xi, please go inside and look. Tell me if anything is wanting, and I will have it seen to."
It was morning, the light full and clear. She stepped inside and at once saw, in the center of the inner courtyard, a peach tree.
And all around the courtyard, a ring of them — pink blossoms open to the air, petals stirring in the breeze, carrying a faint, clean fragrance.
Chief Gao watched Xi Rongyan's expression and, as he led her into the main hall, said: "His Majesty heard that Consort Xi loves peach blossoms and had them brought in and planted just two days ago."
He smiled again: "In my three years serving His Majesty, I have never once seen him go to such lengths for anyone."
The great doors opened slowly, and a breath of settled dust drifted free. Xi Rongyan listened to Chief Gao as she looked out at the spacious interior — and found, to her surprise, that everything had been furnished to her taste.
Gao Yi watched Xi Rongyan from the corner of his eye and continued to lead her forward: "Four rooms connected through, with a small study specially prepared as well. Consort Xi, please look — wherever it does not suit you, I will have it changed."
Xi Rongyan moved through the rooms step by step. Every arrangement was intricate and well-considered — from the small sitting room to the inner chamber, the floors all covered in soft wool rugs, beneath fragrant gauze curtains stood a screen of four folding panels painted with a profusion of blossoms.
The shelves were filled with delicate objects, each one unusual.
Even the maidservants who had followed Xi Rongyan in were left speechless.
They had expected that for a Zhaoyi, only two plain rooms and simple furnishings. Not this — furnished better, and more elegantly, than their young miss's own bedchamber at home.
Until they came to the innermost room: a carved rosewood bed hung with jade ornaments, a mirror of eight treasures on the dressing table, and a crane-shaped lamp strung with eastern pearls.
Xi Rongyan stared for a moment, then turned to Chief Gao.
After a pause, she said: "Everything pleases me."
"Only..."

chapters.title: No One in the Palace Can Compare to Consort Xi
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan's words trailed off.
Chief Gao could, of course, read perfectly well what she was about to say.
A woman barely through the palace gates, already given quarters like these — furnished with such evident care and thought — was this not the favor of a singular place?
If the Emperor had not been worried that bestowing too much too soon would draw too much attention, he would very likely have conferred the rank of Noble Consort outright.
In this inner palace, how many women spent a lifetime yearning for the rank of Noble Consort and never reached it? And this one had only appeared before the Emperor twice, and already had everything.
In truth, Gao Yi himself could not quite make sense of it — the Emperor, a man of such deeply hidden nature, cold and alone in his private heart, choosing to be so singularly different toward the Fourth Young Miss of the Xi family.
He smiled at Xi Rongyan. "His Majesty is presently in the Hall of Diligent Governance. He will come to see you when he is free."
And with that, Gao Yi called for the head attendant of Hanyuan Hall and asked her to introduce the palace servants to Xi Rongyan. He then turned to Xi Rongyan: "You have only just arrived and must be tired. Rest your feet awhile. I will go and report back to His Majesty."
Xi Rongyan knew there were some things she would get no answer to from Chief Gao.
She steadied her thoughts and asked Yuzhu to see Chief Gao out.
Yuzhu complied and walked the Chief to the outer door. Once outside, she produced a large ingot of silver from her sleeve and pressed it into his hands with a smile. "My mistress has only just entered the palace and does not yet know her way about many things. I hope Chief Gao will guide us going forward."
Yuzhu was Lady Xie's own close maidservant — steady and composed, with a measured warmth in her manner that made her words land well.
Gao Yi gave a short laugh and pushed the silver back. "Set your mind at ease. Among all the ladies in this palace, none can compare to Consort Xi."
And with that smile, he went on his way.
Yuzhu did not quite grasp what Chief Gao had meant, but seeing him already at a distance, she could only turn back inside.
Inside the room, Xi Rongyan sat in the great broad chair, listening to the head attendant introduce the palace servants. Hanyuan Hall had seven women in service; with Xi Rongyan's own two added, there were nine in total.
Yuzhu relayed a few instructions on Xi Rongyan's behalf, then asked Baozhu to give out the gifts.
Lady Xie had prepared them well in advance — a prettily carved small box for each person, inside each box a jade hairpin and a small handful of silver coins.
The palace servants exchanged glances and whispered amongst themselves at the generosity of it, then sank quickly to their knees to give thanks.
Xi Rongyan made her way to the inner room. Yuzhu followed close behind and murmured a reminder: "When we came through the gate earlier, a lady from the Empress Dowager's palace came to let us know — it is time to go and pay your respects to the Empress Dowager now."
"After you return from the Empress Dowager, you will need to go and call upon the Empress."
Xi Rongyan already knew she would not have a moment's rest yet.
She sat down before the dressing table and let Baozhu attend to her hair while she asked Yuzhu: "Did you bring the boxes Mother prepared?"
Yuzhu smiled. "Nothing will go amiss, Mistress. I have the one prepared especially for the Empress Dowager right here."
Xi Rongyan turned back to the mirror and studied herself — hairpins straight, makeup simple and clean, everything as orderly and proper as it should be. Then she stood.
She had barely stepped out of the inner room when the head attendant, Attendant Fang, came to speak to her quietly: "The Empress's personal nanny, Nanny Yu, has come to request that the Mistress go to Yongchun Palace."
Yuzhu asked Attendant Fang to go ahead and placate Nanny Yu while she dressed, then bent close to Xi Rongyan's ear: "The Empress's father is the Emperor's most capable and loyal military general, now holding the northern territories. He is the person the Emperor trusts most."
"It would be better to visit the Empress first."
All of this Xi Rongyan already knew — her mother had gone over it with her the previous evening.
When the Emperor returned to the capital from the north, it had been the Empress's father, General Song, who commanded the two thousand soldiers that encircled the imperial city. Her mother had said that General Song had followed the Emperor from his days as a prince — the soldiers of the north were troops the Emperor himself had built and trained, and no one but a man of absolute trust would be given charge of them.
Unless the Empress committed some grave wrong, her position was unassailable.
Xi Rongyan nodded. Her aunt would not blame her for any apparent slight — but the Empress was another matter.
She weighed the options briefly, and settled on calling on the Empress first.
But the moment she stepped out of the hall and was about to send someone ahead to the Empress Dowager's palace to explain, the Empress Dowager's own Attendant Wan arrived in person to escort her.
The moment she saw Xi Rongyan, Attendant Wan smiled warmly. "Please come with me to see the Empress Dowager, Consort Xi. Today the Empress Dowager has known you were entering the palace — she has been waiting since early morning and has much she wishes to say."
Xi Rongyan was in a difficult position. "Nanny Yu from the Empress's palace came just now to call me there first. Please allow me to pay my respects to the Empress before going to see the Empress Dowager."
Attendant Wan smiled. "The Empress's matter can wait a little. Consort Xi need not worry — the Empress Dowager will send word to the Empress's palace. The Empress will not take offense, nor will she fault you for it."
"The Empress Dowager has been waiting for you since the morning."
Hearing this, Xi Rongyan hesitated briefly — yet she had already made a prior agreement with her aunt, and so she followed Attendant Wan toward Cining Palace.
—
In Yongchun Palace, Empress Song Helan sat composed in the seat of honor. Beside her, incense drifted from the altar. Her expression was serene. Her long lacquered nails moved over the white cat resting in her lap, and she listened in silence to the voices rising and falling below her, her eyes showing not the faintest ripple of emotion.
She heard Consort Huang's voice: "Is it not simply because she has the Empress Dowager to back her?"
"On her very first day in the palace, she makes even the Empress send her people to fetch her. And now we are all sitting here waiting for one person — what an air of importance she has."
Noble Lady Tan beside her smiled, her words carrying a faint edge: "And does she not have an air of importance? She is something else entirely."
"The Gu family business was barely two months past, and here she is, rushing into the palace. Eight to one she had the Empress Dowager arrange it for her. With the Empress Dowager as her aunt, she doesn't even care about putting the Empress in her place."
She then looked toward Consort Wang and said pointedly: "She arrived and was already given the rank of Zhaoyi. I hear the Emperor has placed her in the main hall of Hanyuan Hall. My sister here, who enjoys such favor, never had this."
Consort Wang pressed her fingers tight and kept a mild smile as she glanced at Noble Lady Tan: "She is the Empress Dowager's niece — how can I compare?"
The Empress had not spoken throughout. She had neither shown any inclination to take a side, nor made any move to silence the others.
She had been at the Emperor's side since before he was even a prince. She knew better than anyone — the Emperor would never defer to anyone else's wishes. Whether the Empress Dowager had arranged this or not, if the Emperor wished someone to enter the palace, that person entered the palace.
She thought of something she had said to the Emperor the previous night.
She had said that having Xi Rongyan housed in Hanyuan Hall did not accord with propriety. A Zhaoyi being placed in the main hall of Guanju Palace was an obvious show of favoritism that would stir the inner palace.
She had only been speaking in her capacity as Empress, counseling against the disruption of the inner palace's balance — however much or little personal feeling was behind it, she felt it had to be said.
But the man seated high and cold at the writing desk — his black robe with its gold key-pattern trim all of a piece with the chill — had not even dropped his gaze on her. He had simply said, cold and quiet: "Leave."
Like two knives pressed directly into her heart.
So much for what people called the bond forged in youth.
She still did not know what made Xi Rongyan different. This year the spring selection of new consorts had been cancelled outright, and only the Xi family had received a decree.

chapters.title: What Expression Did She Have When She Entered the Palace?
chapters.content:
Song Helan's thoughts drifted back to the day of the Flower Festival.
Gao Yi had placed a bamboo slip in her hand — the verse, he had said, had pleased the Emperor.
She understood the meaning. She read it over and found it perfectly ordinary — but she had selected it nonetheless.
Perhaps this verse might happen to catch the Emperor's eye.
Looking back now, the signs had all been there.
The Emperor, who never attended the Flower Festival, had gone that day without a word of notice.
The Emperor, who never concerned himself with such matters, had sent Gao Yi to specially arrange the gift of wine.
Xi Rongyan entering the palace had perhaps been planned by the Emperor all along — quietly, and with considerable care.
Below her, the chatter was still going on. As Empress, she needed to keep matters in hand.
In truth, her informants had already brought word to her ear: Xi Rongyan had not come because the Empress Dowager had called her. She would be along presently, and the Empress Dowager would send word.
For Xi Rongyan to go first to the Empress Dowager — who outranked even her — was not wrong. It was not a grave matter, nor had anything gone amiss.
But at this moment she had no intention of explaining on Xi Rongyan's behalf.
She only sighed, and in a tone of warmth and tolerance addressed those below: "Consort Xi has only just entered the palace today. It is no matter if she is a little late."
"We will all be sisters going forward — treat her well."
"And take care of her."
"Since she has not yet arrived, there is no need for you all to wait. You may go."
The others had chattered hoping the Empress would give Xi Rongyan some punishment, and had not expected her to let it pass so easily.
Xi Rongyan had the Empress Dowager behind her — but the Empress had spent seven years at the Emperor's side, had followed him from the north to the capital, and in all the inner palace, no woman's bond with the Emperor could rival that. Moreover, Xi Rongyan's silent disregard of the Empress's summons — whatever its actual cause — was a fault in itself.
Furthermore, Xi Rongyan's sudden appearance had given all of them a faint sense of unease.
Because it was said that Gao Yi had come personally to receive her — and what that meant, they all understood, though they preferred not to say it aloud.
Everyone's expressions were unreadable. On the surface they all acquiesced and withdrew in orderly fashion.
Once outside, they could not help but fall into whispers.
Noble Consort Xian was the last to stay behind. When the others had all gone, she stepped close to the Empress and called softly: "Elder Cousin."
Song Helan glanced at Noble Consort Xian and kept her same expression of detached calm: "Say no more of this."
Noble Consort Xian was taken aback and could not help asking: "Elder Cousin, why did you arrange for Xi Rongyan to stay in Hanyuan Hall?"
"Even the Empress Dowager cannot interfere in the Emperor's inner palace, can she?"
Song Helan sighed. A trace of bitterness showed deep in her eyes.
The Emperor, who had never once involved himself in the affairs of the inner palace, was willing to break every rule of propriety for Xi Rongyan.
The Empress, holding the seal of the inner palace, was herself something of a joke.
She looked at Song Ningyu and said slowly: "In the days ahead, do not provoke Xi Rongyan."
Song Ningyu started, then said with some defiance: "What is there to fear from her? She is just the Empress Dowager's niece. Why should she be untouchable?"
"My father and uncle still hold the north's sixteen border prefectures. That is the most vital stretch of the front line against Northern Yan."
"And in the whole inner palace, only my elder cousin has given the Emperor a prince. Who would dare not respect elder cousin?"
Song Helan's brow furrowed slightly. Her eyes held a look of quiet warning as she said to Song Ningyu: "Listen to me. There is no need for us to act."
She narrowed those calm eyes, and a chill settled into their depths: "Wait and watch."
Song Ningyu pressed her lips together.
In her eyes, Xi Rongyan was nothing worth worrying about.
Over these three years, the Emperor's visits to the inner palace had been few enough to count on one hand — and he came most often to her elder cousin.
Of all these women, only her elder cousin had given the Emperor a prince.
Though the Emperor had yet to name a Crown Prince, that was only a matter of time.
Xi Rongyan, pushed in by the Empress Dowager — whatever stir she made now was no more than the Emperor showing courtesy to the Empress Dowager's face. Before long she would be crawling back to her elder cousin's feet with her tail between her legs.
And yet, thinking this, Song Ningyu still felt a prick of irritation.
When her elder cousin had married the Emperor, her father had sent her into the palace as a side consort as well. She had believed she might stand at the side of that fine, commanding man, just as her elder cousin did.
But in five long, slow years, that man had never once looked at her directly.
She understood by now that she would never be favored by the Emperor. She could only lean on her cousin for protection and keep her footing in the inner palace.
She knew her elder cousin's abilities — wit and calculation all surpassing her own — and that their interests were bound together. She had only to follow her cousin's lead.
She pressed close to the Empress again, still a little unwilling: "The Emperor never visits me. Sister, can you at least let me have a child in the end?"
"Even a princess would do."
Song Helan looked at Song Ningyu and patted her shoulder in quiet silence: "Be patient. Give it time."
Song Ningyu's expression faltered. Every time she raised this, her elder cousin said to be patient. How much longer must she be patient?
She still felt some resentment — but in the end, she dared not say it aloud.
—
In the Hall of Diligent Governance, Wei Qi's tall figure reclined in the great chair, a shaft of clear morning light through the wide windows falling across the corner of his dark dragon robe. The gold threading glimmered in and out.
His cold eyes flicked sideways. Gao Yi's heart lurched, and he dropped immediately to his knees: "This servant also did not expect Consort Xi to linger so long with the Empress Dowager. And this servant could not very well drag the Consort away from under the Empress Dowager's nose."
Heaven knew that the Emperor had decided, on an impulse, to go share the midday meal with Consort Xi. Had he said so earlier, Consort Xi would certainly have been waiting for him in Guanju Palace.
Wei Qi pressed his lips together, one palm propped against his brow, in the extraordinary stillness of the hall. Then, in a low voice, unexpected: "What expression did she have when she entered the palace?"
As the question left him, Wei Qi shut his eyes. And in the darkness behind them, he saw Xi Rongyan, tears in her eyes, kneeling in the snow, begging him to let her go.
She had always begged him.
No matter how he coaxed, she could never be soothed.
Tender and gentle — that had not worked. Stern — that had not worked either.
Her eyes held only her child, and the husband who had already died.
He had never been a patient man by nature, yet for her he had conceded again and again and again.
He sank deeper into his thoughts, and his expression grew darker.
Near him, Gao Yi's careful voice came: "When Consort Xi first got into the palanquin, she was reluctant to leave her family and cried a little. But when she arrived and saw all that Your Majesty had prepared, her face was full of happiness."
"She even mentioned she adores peach blossoms, and that the furnishings were exactly to her liking. This servant thought Consort Xi could see the care Your Majesty had taken."
Gao Yi had barely finished speaking when a low, cold sound of contempt came from above. His back went cold immediately. He pressed his forehead back to the floor and braced himself for the Emperor's judgment.
He wished he could give himself two hard slaps — he deserved it for talking too much. The Emperor had asked like that, and he must have known the answer in his heart already.
But afterward there was only a long, lasting silence.
No one could say how long it stretched, before a quiet voice came again: "How long did she cry?"
Gao Yi paused, then answered quickly: "Only a little while in the palanquin. By the time she was inside the palace, she had stopped."
"This servant believes Consort Xi cried only because she was reluctant to leave her family."
Wei Qi pressed his lips together.
He understood. Xi Rongyan still did not want to be here.
He had come back too late this time.
If only it had been a little sooner...

chapters.title: I Know. It Is Not Your Fault.
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan did not leave the Empress Dowager's quarters until the afternoon.
She then hurried on toward the Empress's palace.
Walking the corridor, she kept her head slightly bowed, thinking over what her aunt had said.
Her aunt had told her that the great families were losing ground, and that the Emperor was moving to strip them of their power — so her entering the palace was not a bad thing.
One never knew when the knife hovering above the Xi family might fall. She must strive to earn the Emperor's favor.
The Emperor's inner palace held many women who had been daughters of loyal followers from the northern campaigns. In the three years since his accession, he had added very few new consorts.
So long as she bore a child, the Empress Dowager would find a way to support her child's claim to the position of Crown Prince.
Xi Rongyan knew the Empress already had one prince, not yet six years old. The Empress and the Emperor had been matched by the late Emperor's decree, companions since youth, and in the whole inner palace, only that one prince.
Today her aunt had held her hand and spoken gravely — in the inner palace, wishing to stand apart from the fray was not possible. Others would draw you in whether you wanted it or not.
The Empress might not hold that position forever.
Whoever's son became Crown Prince would be the final victor.
She understood her aunt's meaning well enough.
Once she gave birth to a prince, the real contest would begin.
Even if she chose not to compete, others would.
She was so absorbed in thought, her head bowed, that she did not notice the palanquin approaching from the other side.
It was only when she heard a sharp, cold scoff that she looked up.
On the palanquin sat a young woman in deep teal silk, her hair full of pearl pins, pendant ornaments swaying with the motion. A bewitching face — red lips vivid, a cool disdain in her gaze as she looked Xi Rongyan up and down.
Then her eyes made a slow, dismissive sweep, and she spoke with faint mockery: "And who are you, from which palace? You have quite the air about you — you dare to simply ignore me."
Xi Rongyan did not know who this was. Fortunately, she had brought a Hanyuan Hall court lady with her, and the lady bent to whisper quickly in her ear.
The woman on the palanquin was Noble Consort Xian.
The Empress's own first cousin.
Second daughter of the second branch of Zhongyong Marquisate.
She was several years older than Xi Rongyan, and had been in the Emperor's palace for a long time — though their paths within the city had scarcely crossed.
By rank, Xi Rongyan did owe the Noble Consort a bow.
Thinking she had indeed been somewhat neglectful, and that palace rules were strict — she had been about to bow and apologize when the Noble Consort suddenly stepped off the palanquin and came to stand before her.
The Noble Consort was tall. Her chin raised high, she looked at Xi Rongyan with barely concealed contempt, then reached out a hand — fingernails encased in long gilded sheaths — and gripped Xi Rongyan's chin, turning it left and right as if appraising goods. Her tone was mocking: "Tsk. Just look at this fragile little vixen. Do you think that by scheming your way into the palace, you'll win the Emperor's affection? You have the nerve to slight the Empress."
"Today I will teach you a lesson on the Empress's behalf."
The grip on her chin was heavy — those long nails pressed into Xi Rongyan's skin. Xi Rongyan's expression shifted slightly.
She knew the Zhongyong Marquisate was riding high these days, deep in the Emperor's trust, and had followed him since before he was even a prince.
Her aunt had told her today that when the Crown Prince fell from grace, the Xi family and certain great houses had spoken out in the Crown Prince's defense and had spoken slightingly of the Emperor when he was still the Third Prince. The Emperor might not have forgotten.
Now General Song's household secured the frontier; every member bore merit and rank. The Empress of the main palace was Song's eldest daughter of the primary line. The Song family truly had every right to its arrogance.
If it came to reasoning it out, palace rules were strict — she had not yet learned all of them fully, and the Empress might not take her side. Moreover the Noble Consort outranked her.
Xi Rongyan turned all of it over several times in her mind, and then she saw the Noble Consort's hand with its fitted finger guards suddenly raised — if those sharp sheaths came down across her face, they would leave two lines of blood.
Yuzhu and Baozhu, standing behind Xi Rongyan, also felt their faces change — they had not expected the Noble Consort to actually strike.
Xi Rongyan looked at the descending hand, and in that moment recalled her aunt's words.
There was no such thing as tranquility in the inner palace — the camaraderie of sisters.
Though she wished for stillness, the wind would not stop. From the first day she entered the palace, she may have already become a thorn in someone's side.
For three years, the inner palace had been almost entirely the Song family's domain. The women who entered new almost always fell in line with them — or else they were suppressed and driven out. Everyone knew she was the Empress Dowager's niece. She was bound to be a target.
Now she understood it, in her own person.
The grip on her chin was too forceful — Xi Rongyan could not simply stand and allow herself to be struck.
She raised her hand and blocked the Noble Consort's arm, saying quickly: "I did not intentionally ignore the Noble Consort earlier. If the Noble Consort does this without even allowing an explanation — never mind whether it is within the palace rules or not — is there truly no room here to speak?"
Song Ningyu had not expected Xi Rongyan to dare block her, and gave a cold laugh: "And today you ignored the Empress's summons — is that not a grave offense?"
"My elder cousin is kind and let it pass. But I cannot stomach it. I mean to teach you something."
She then called to her attendants: "Hold her hands."
Baozhu's expression changed. Seeing the Noble Consort's hand about to come down again, she threw herself in front of Xi Rongyan — and the nail sheaths raked across her cheek, leaving a thin cut.
Then from nearby, Gao Yi's voice came sharp and urgent: "Stop!"
Song Ningyu startled at the sound and turned quickly — just in time to see Gao Yi running up, and behind him, at a measured pace, the Emperor, face unreadable.
She instantly let her people release Xi Rongyan and stepped back.
Gao Yi took in the scene and felt his own heart leap.
The Emperor had only just learned that Consort Xi had left the Empress Dowager's palace, and had come at once to arrange a chance encounter. Instead he had walked into this.
He quickly went to Xi Rongyan and asked: "Is Consort Xi all right?"
Song Ningyu looked at this and felt the ground shift.
She was not favored in the palace, but her rank was one of the highest among the consorts — and in any case no one in the inner palace enjoyed much favor at all. Gao Yi had always shown her a degree of courtesy on account of all that.
Yet now Gao Yi had come over and stood directly before Xi Rongyan without so much as a glance at her.
Her eyes widened. She caught sight of the approaching Emperor from the corner of her eye and immediately flung herself toward him in a rush of wailing: "Your Majesty, please do justice for your consort!"
"Consort Xi not only looked right past me, but today when the Empress sent for her, she ignored the Empress entirely and has not appeared even now."
"She relies on being the Empress Dowager's niece and does not even deign to regard the Empress."
"Your Majesty, please..."
Her voice cut off mid-sentence. She had looked up — and met a pair of eyes, merciless and cold as ice.
She quailed. Her hands shook. Her body took two involuntary steps backward.
She had seen the Emperor in his coldest moods more times than she could count — cold enough that she had never dared to cajole him even in her most playful moments.
In that moment, she felt cold to the bone.
In the whole inner palace, not a single woman dared to act capriciously in the Emperor's presence. Even her elder cousin trod carefully around him.
On Xi Rongyan's side, hearing Song Ningyu's accusations, her heart tightened. She knew the Song family had the inner palace in their grip — perhaps even with the Emperor's tolerance. But she could not simply let herself be falsely accused.
She quickly moved to kneel and explain — and before she had even gone down, she was gathered into a warm embrace.
When Xi Rongyan came to her senses, dark brocade filled her vision.
A broad hand pressed at the small of her back. A low, tender voice came from above her head: "It is all right."
Xi Rongyan was still. Slowly she looked up — and met a pair of soft eyes.
Those eyes that by nature held such sharpness — the cutting brow, the almond-shaped gaze — were gentle now, and unexpectedly kind.
She thought he looked gentle. And yet she thought it strange.
Her brother and father had said the Emperor was not a gentle man — to always observe her place.
She was still lost in thought when she heard herself begin to speak: "This subject did not intend to slight the Empress — when the Empress sent her ladies, the Empress Dowager had already..."
The sentence was not finished before she heard the Emperor say, low and quiet: "I know. It is not your fault."

chapters.title: I Will Stay in Hanyuan Hall Tonight
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan's heart gave a startled beat.
Then her body seemed to lighten — and she found herself lifted, cradled sideways in the Emperor's arms.
This single moment left every person present speechless.
Song Ningyu's face went white with shock.
For she knew, better than anyone, how cold a man the Emperor was.
No matter how much any of them tried to please him, the Emperor had always been composed and severe, as though no one had ever entered those cold eyes at all.
He had never been moved. Not by anyone.
Not once.
She had tried so many times to win his favor, and yet even drawing near to him had always made her feel cold.
And now — the Emperor was holding a woman who had been in the palace for less than a day, and holding her openly, in front of everyone.
She felt unsteady. She stared at this scene, something unnamed and aching stirring in her chest.
Xi Rongyan had not expected it either.
The color drained slightly from her face. Her hands went helplessly to the Emperor's shoulders, her mouth open a little, clearly at a loss and alarmed.
Wei Qi saw it all, and pressed his lips together. He held her gaze — her eyes unsteady, the silver-white earrings glimpsing in and out of the dark hair — and knew she was still afraid of him.
He softened his voice: "I will carry you back."
Xi Rongyan did not even know how to begin to speak. She could only press tight to the Emperor's chest as he truly began walking, her fingers clutching the handkerchief in her hands, her heart in quiet turmoil.
Being looked at by so many pairs of eyes — she was, in the end, deeply shy. She half-turned her face and buried it against the Emperor's shoulder, shifting her body slightly, her voice almost too small to hear: "This subject..."
"This subject can walk on her own."
The pink-grey skirt swayed against the dragon robe. White embroidered slippers peeked out a demure, pointed inch.
The fair nape of her neck was warm with a faint sweetness. In her yielding shyness there was a soft, spring-soft allure. Wei Qi looked down at her, faintly as one coaxes a small cat that will not quite submit: "Stay still."
Only — on the fine face that Xi Rongyan could not see, his expression had gone cold and flat. Those long eyes swept once, glacially, to Song Ningyu standing stricken and staring, then once to Gao Yi — and then he carried Xi Rongyan away.
Gao Yi understood perfectly what the Emperor meant.
The Emperor had always kept his feelings from showing — his moods unreadable. To carry Consort Xi in his arms like the most precious thing in the world, here where all could see — what that announced, Gao Yi understood with perfect clarity.
The Emperor was telling every woman in this inner palace: Xi Rongyan is the person closest to his heart. Do not harbor any ill intentions toward her.
Anyone who dared to touch Xi Rongyan — today's Noble Consort was the first warning.
When the Emperor had taken Consort Xi far enough away, Gao Yi turned at his leisure to the Noble Consort, still stunned and stricken, wearing the cool indifference that the Emperor himself always wore: "Noble Consort Xian has behaved improperly in the inner palace and has given offense. Effective immediately, she is to be confined to Huayang Palace, and to receive fifteen blows."
Song Ningyu looked at Gao Yi in horror. Then, as understanding broke, she threw herself to her knees, the pendants in her hair swinging violently. She sobbed and pleaded: "Chief Gao, I must see the Emperor."
"It was clearly Xi Rongyan who offended me first. I am Noble Consort — what is she, a Zhaoyi, to me? Why should I be the one punished?"
Gao Yi's expression remained flat. He stepped back one pace and let the guards behind him muffle Song Ningyu's cries and drag her away.
On the other side, Xi Rongyan, still in the Emperor's arms, heard faintly the sound of weeping from behind. She could not help shifting slightly, wanting to turn and look — and then a hand at her waist gave a soft, deliberate press.
The intimate touch sent a little dizziness through her. She knew those eyes were on her. She did not dare look up, her heart uneasy. From the moment all this had started until now, she felt as though she were still wandering in a dream.
The Emperor's scent surrounded her. It was nothing like Yunyu gege's scent — that faint, refined fragrance that had always gently settled her restless heart. The Emperor's scent was different. It pressed in from all sides, filling her senses, and always left her rattled and uncertain.
As though it meant to wrap itself entirely around her and leave no part of her free.
Wei Qi looked down at Xi Rongyan's face half-hidden against him, at her closed lashes trembling, and tightened his hand in silence, his expression darkening where she could not see.
The rest of the walk home was finished at Xi Rongyan's quiet, earnest request — Wei Qi set her down and let her walk.
He held her hand along the palace corridor. Between them, silence. Not a word from either side.
Xi Rongyan was quiet because she did not know what to say to the Emperor, and was too uneasy to speak.
Wei Qi did want to speak, but was not the kind of man who was easy with small talk. He turned the thought over for a while, and from the corner of his eye caught the subtle furrow of Xi Rongyan's fine brows, and in the end said nothing.
This stretch of corridor was agony for Xi Rongyan. She thought it over many times in her heart, and finally worked up her courage to explain the earlier matter clearly.
Wei Qi gave a hum of acknowledgment, his voice gentle — but offered nothing more.
Xi Rongyan could not read the Emperor's intention, and said softly: "This subject has not yet paid her respects to the Empress since entering the palace. I really should go call on her now."
Wei Qi's fingers traced over Xi Rongyan's soft palm. Then he spoke: "I have already sent someone to the Empress to explain. You have only just entered the palace and are tired. Tomorrow will be soon enough."
He let his gaze settle on Xi Rongyan. Seeing her expression shift with unease — something hovering on her lips, wanting and not wanting to be said — she looked to him like a startled sparrow that would always be easily frightened. The corner of his mouth curved.
Soon they reached Hanyuan Hall. Wei Qi stopped at the hall door and did not go in. He only drew his fingers along the fine skin of Xi Rongyan's cheek, looking at her — her brows and eyes lovely, the dark brows gently arched, that pair of eyes lowered shyly — and felt a tenderness rise in his chest.
He could not help but think of the moment she had held a dagger pressed against him, resolute and unmoving.
That woman who was always so timid and soft and gentle — when she truly dug in her heels, it was equally enough to break one apart.
He cut off the thought. His palm settled at her soft waist. He bent toward her slightly, his gaze deep and shadowed, close enough that it became something charged and almost tender. His voice came out low and hoarse without meaning to: "I will stay in Hanyuan Hall tonight."
Such a brief sentence, and yet it sent Xi Rongyan's heart crashing and cresting like waves.
She did not dare show it on her face. She prepared quickly to give her reverent thanks.
But the hand at her waist drew her in against the chest before her. She felt a hand settle quietly on her back, smoothing and soothing. The voice from above was warm and gentle: "Do not be afraid. Simply wait for me."
The Emperor's voice was so calm and kind. Xi Rongyan found herself wondering, bewildered, why the world outside believed the Emperor to be so cruel.
Lost in the thought, she watched the Emperor fall silent and then turn and leave. His retreating figure in the corridor was tall and upright, growing smaller and smaller in the distance.

chapters.title: Shall We Retire Now?
chapters.content:
Back at the Hall of Diligent Governance, Wei Qi clasped his hands behind his back. Gao Yi hurried to report on the matter of the Noble Consort.
Wei Qi stood at the window looking out, silent. After a long pause: "Move her to Yanqiu Palace. Strip her of her title and demote her to Zhaoyi. No visitors are to be permitted."
Gao Yi's breath caught.
Sent to Yanqiu Palace — that was the same as sending her to the cold palace.
At that moment a report came from outside: a letter had arrived from the north.
The north was currently at war. Dispatches had been arriving without pause of late, and the court spoke of little else beyond the situation at the northern front.
In his years as a border prince, Wei Qi had fought for many years and reclaimed seven cities. Now on the throne, there was still more territory to hold and defend.
Gao Yi watched the Emperor's expression and quickly went to retrieve the letter.
—
In Hanyuan Hall, Xi Rongyan settled in the inner chamber and drew Baozhu close at once. She looked at the cut on Baozhu's cheek with reddened eyes.
Baozhu, seeing her mistress distressed, quickly said: "Nothing serious, my Lady. Chief Gao gave me a salve just now. It will be healed in no time."
Xi Rongyan looked at the vial in Baozhu's hands. The sorrow in her eyes did not lift: "And this is only the beginning."
Yuzhu spoke from beside them to console her: "As long as my Lady makes no mistakes, and as the Empress Dowager said — the Emperor chose to bring you into the palace, so he must favor you."
"Win the Emperor's heart properly, and everything else will follow in its own time."
Behind them, the light shifted through the window. Beside the carved beams, an incense burner curled a thread of smoke. Within the layered gauze curtains, the figure in pink moved with quiet composure. The white handkerchief between her fingers twisted and tightened.
Lotus blossoms were worked into the folds of the layered skirt. The jade pin in Xi Rongyan's dark hair was clear and cool. One hand rested on the low table. She shut her eyes and thought of the last words her aunt had said before she left.
Her aunt had told her: once inside the palace, there was only pressing forward. There was no way back.
Imperial favor was quick to fade — but what women in the inner palace fought for was glory, a capable prince to lean on, and in the end a peaceful old age, a position no one could shake, watching new faces enter the palace from a place of serene remove.
She sat a while, her thoughts drifting, and then thought again of the peach blossom hairpin Yunyu gege had given her.
He had carved it himself, cut by cut.
She rose and went to the dressing table, took the peach blossom hairpin from the box. The pink jade glowed softly in the light — transparent and luminous. She looked at it for a long time, and at last felt her heart settle.
When evening came, the sky not yet fully dark, Yuzhu drew her aside with great seriousness and offered careful, hushed instruction. She pressed a bound booklet into Xi Rongyan's hands and murmured: "My Lady, please look through this carefully. Do not be afraid when the time comes."
"The Emperor seems quite cold, but I believe he does favor you."
"My Lady need only let herself go a little — bear through it, and it will pass."
Yuzhu sighed and bent to look at Xi Rongyan's nervous eyes: "I have made inquiries. The Emperor visits the inner palace only once or twice a month. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. My Lady must not let it slip."
"If tonight does not go well, it will be very difficult to have this chance again."
"Even with the Empress Dowager's help, you must do your own part."
Xi Rongyan felt as though she had been bound to a post and set over a flame — she truly had no ability to decide any of this herself.
Even though her heart was full of trembling dread, she could not make herself say she was afraid.
She gripped the booklet Yuzhu had pressed into her hands. Her mother had already shown her its contents — seeing it again now, her palms went cold with shyness and nerves.
Her slender finger rested on one of the pages, and Yuzhu patiently guided her: "Men also enjoy it when a woman takes the initiative. If my Lady is more forthcoming at the right moment, the Emperor may be pleased."
The rosy flush had already spread to the tips of her ears. She looked up at Yuzhu, eyes full of anxiety: "Yuzhu, I..."
Yuzhu could see her mistress's nerves and placed a hand on her shoulder, saying quietly: "Do not be afraid, my Lady. Just remember what I told you. You are wonderful in every way — only your courage is a little small."
"As long as you are not afraid tonight, the Emperor will certainly like you."
In the lamplight, Xi Rongyan's face glowed soft and shifting, her gentle brows unfurrowed, the delicate beauty of a woman with a natural air of soft shyness. Even Yuzhu was briefly taken in by the sight of her — she could not believe the Emperor would not feel tenderness at the sight.
Just then Baozhu rushed in, slightly breathless: "A eunuch just came to tell us the Emperor will arrive shortly."
"We must go out to receive the Emperor."
Yuzhu nodded quickly, made one last careful check of Xi Rongyan's appearance and whispered two more instructions, then took her arm and walked her out.
When Xi Rongyan stood at the palace gate, the Emperor had already arrived.
The palace lanterns on either side lit his face in wavering light. As the palanquin settled and the tall dark figure stepped toward her, it was like an enormous dark net slowly enfolding her whole.
Something irrational surged up inside her — a terror that felt strangely familiar, as though she had lived this moment countless times before, and each time been just as afraid.
The tall figure drew nearer and nearer, and she took an instinctive step back.
The moment she realized what she had done, her face went pale.
Wei Qi also stopped, quite still. The hand he had extended to take hers stilled as well.
In the darkness he looked into her eyes — the same eyes he knew so well, full of fear and unease — and pressed down the anger and the shadow that threatened to surface.
He did not understand. Why was she afraid of him even now?
The night wind moved the hem of her skirt. Wei Qi drew a slow breath and stepped toward her again.
He did not reproach her. When she finally looked up in her anxiety, he tilted his head and smiled down at her — a small, quiet reassurance — and then took her hand and walked with her inside, his voice as gentle as he could make it: "Were the dishes to your liking this afternoon?"
Xi Rongyan walked close beside the Emperor and answered softly: "Yes, they were."
They truly had been.
Every dish had been one Xi Rongyan had loved since girlhood. When she had seen them that afternoon, she had not known whether it was coincidence or something more — even the flavors were just as she remembered.
Wei Qi gave a small smile and led Xi Rongyan directly into the inner chamber.
He guided her to sit with him on the daybed. The palace servants inside all quietly retreated behind the curtains.
Baozhu peered through the thin gauze, watching — so anxious on her mistress's behalf she might well have been more anxious than her mistress herself.
The two of them sat close together, their robes touching, and Xi Rongyan's hand was still held in the Emperor's. She was nervous too.
The last time she had seen him she had already been frightened — but then she had known she would be going home soon. Now, drifting in a daze, she had somehow become the Emperor's consort. Even with everything Yuzhu had told her earlier, her mind now held nothing but blankness.
She did not even dare look directly at the Emperor. She could only steady herself as best she could and reach to pour him tea. She held the cup and offered it to him carefully: "Tea for Your Majesty."
Wei Qi raised one brow slightly, watching the fingertips at the rim of the white jade cup. He took in every tremor of her nerves. He accepted the cup — and set it aside.
This startled Xi Rongyan. She thought she had not served him well enough, or that the tea did not suit him.
But her aunt had said the Emperor liked Mingxue tea, and Yuzhu had specifically brewed it. Surely nothing had gone wrong.
She was about to apologize when in the next moment a hand settled at her waist, and in one smooth motion drew her forward and into his lap.
Beyond the gauze curtain, Baozhu's face broke into a delighted smile.
So the Emperor truly did like her mistress. He had barely sat down before he was already holding her.
She finally let out a full breath of relief.
Beside her, Yuzhu was watching Xi Rongyan's still-stiff posture with a face full of worry, afraid the Emperor would lose patience.
Wei Qi's gaze swept the two figures peering through the curtain from beyond, then dropped to the person in his arms.
He met her flustered, unsteady eyes. His gaze moved, inch by careful inch, from the fine bridge of her nose downward, coming to rest on the full curve of her lips.
His gaze went dark. His chest pressed slightly forward toward her. His eyes returned to hers. His throat moved. His voice came low: "Shall we retire now?"

chapters.title: Attending the Emperor's Bed
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan had only just been startled by the Emperor's actions when she was left stunned again by his words.
From the tone of his voice, it sounded as though he was asking for her opinion.
This was entirely at odds with what she had initially imagined.
She had not expected the Emperor to ask her at all.
After a brief, blank-minded pause, she dazedly nodded her head. She naturally dared not defy the Emperor's wishes. "Then this concubine shall attend Your Majesty and help you change."

As she said this, Xi Rongyan moved to rise from the Emperor's lap.
But the fingers at her waist held her in place, showing no intention of letting go. She saw only the Emperor's deep, dark eyes fixed intently upon her, and then his low voice came: "If you are frightened, I can simply hold you without doing anything."
Xi Rongyan was stunned once again.
The Emperor was completely unlike the one she had imagined — unlike even the one she had heard described at the Empress Dowager's palace.
The Emperor actually cared about her feelings. He actually cared that she was afraid.
Wei Qi watched Xi Rongyan's expression intently. He patted her back lightly with his palm, holding her small and delicate figure against himself, and gently soothed her: "I know you're frightened, Yan'er. I will not force you."
A strange feeling flooded Xi Rongyan's heart. She was at a loss, yet she found the Emperor's words soft and unhurried, and for just a moment, this version of the Emperor resembled her Yunyu-gege.
The Emperor called her Yan'er, just as Yunyu-gege had once called her "Little Sister Yan."
Her chin rested on the Emperor's broad shoulder, her fingers lightly settled at his waist. She understood that once she had entered the palace, she needed to accept her circumstances — she still had her family to think of, and could not act willfully.
Xi Rongyan closed her eyes and said softly, "This concubine is not frightened."
The delicate jade-green eardrops trembled, brushing against Wei Qi's jaw. He silently pressed his lips together and pulled the figure in his arms even closer.
Her soft body and lingering fragrance were just as he remembered — they made him want to press her into himself.
But he restrained himself, suppressing the desire he felt for her.
He thought of the first time he had taken her.
She had wept terribly.
Her blows against his chest were not strong.
She kept her nails trimmed short and rounded, so even when she scratched his face, it did not hurt.
But she had struggled desperately.
Crying out and refusing to cooperate in the slightest.
In the end, he had grown furious, binding her wrists to the bedposts and pressing down on her in a manner akin to venting his rage.
But she kept crying out in pain, tears pouring endlessly from those soft eyes of hers. The sight of it enraged him; the sound of it enraged him.
She had already borne a child — how could she keep crying out in pain?
She simply did not want to be with him. She did not want him to touch her.
The sound of her crying out in pain felt like an insult to his dignity.
He had used more force, lashing out at her and at himself all the same.
After that, every time she saw him, all she felt was fear.
Later, when he saw that her lips had been bitten until they bled, he finally understood that the pain had been real.
Still later, he came to understand that the women in his harem dared not cry out in pain — but they were in pain too.
He had never before considered a woman's feelings. He did not know what it meant to be tender, and he had come to realize he was not like other men.
Now, however, he had no desire to let Xi Rongyan resist him again.
Having learned his lesson, he would wait patiently until she could willingly accept him.
He also knew that for a woman, the first time was far more unbearable. Though he feared Xi Rongyan's resistance, he feared even more that he could not give her a better experience — as it had been in the previous life, where neither of them had ever found any ease. Now, all he needed was for her to slowly accept him in her heart.
After all, now he was her first man.
Wei Qi carried Xi Rongyan toward the bed. But he did not have her undress him. He bent down and gently caressed her face, and said in a low, husky voice: "You and I are like an ordinary husband and wife. You need not be afraid of me."
"No matter what you do, I will not blame you."
"Even within the palace, you may do as you please."
Xi Rongyan's mind wandered, lost in those words — ordinary husband and wife. She could not come back to herself.
Why would the Emperor say such things to her?
She fidgeted anxiously, pinching at the hem of her sleeve, but did not dare to respond.
By no measure could she and the Emperor be called husband and wife. If she agreed to it, would that not be coveting the position of Empress?
Seeing Xi Rongyan dazed and silent, staring at him blankly as though she could not process his words, Wei Qi understood she would not believe him now. But that was all right — they had a long time ahead of them.
One day she would believe.
Wei Qi lowered his eyes, cradling her face, his thumb gently brushing the corner of her lips. His dark eyes gazed straight at the pair of eyes he had longed for day and night, and a storm raged within him.
He very much wanted to kiss her lips.
Although he knew she would no longer look at him with hatred and resist him, he still asked with a trace of caution: "May I kiss you?"
Xi Rongyan felt herself nearly drowning in the Emperor's gentle and deep gaze. Her cheeks began to burn, and she gave a quiet nod, though her fingers clenched together with nervousness.
The moment Xi Rongyan nodded, Wei Qi could not wait any longer. He bent down eagerly, prying her lips apart and advancing with a little more urgency than he had intended.
But he abruptly stilled when he heard her let out a soft sound.
He saw those ink-dark brows furrow, as though she did not particularly enjoy it.
Wei Qi understood that he still could not conceal the desire he felt for her. He had lost her once before, and the emotion of having her returned to him made him unable to restrain himself.
He cast his eyes downward, used his palm to cover Xi Rongyan's eyes, his burning gaze roving freely over her as he took much more care with his movements.
The palace servants waiting outside knew what was happening within, and made themselves scarce, going to lower the bed curtains.
It was only the hour of xu — the Emperor had come and led their mistress straight to the bed the moment he arrived. None of them had expected that.
Baozhu was anxious. Though she could not see inside, she was curious and pressed her ear toward the inner chamber.
She could only catch a few faint, scattered sounds — soft and indistinct, impossible to make out — and had no idea what was truly happening within.
In the inner chamber, upon the bed, Xi Rongyan had long since been disheveled beneath the Emperor. She was dazed from his kisses, her eyes shimmering with a hazy film of tears. The figure before her was blurred, only that one pair of eyes standing out with strange familiarity.
That gaze upon her body seemed to carry a chill, yet also seemed full of deep feeling.
She could not tell which it was. She only felt that her body had gone soft, and the Emperor's husky voice drifted into her ear: "Does Yan'er like this?"
Xi Rongyan could not answer.
She was forced to tilt her head back, her lips parted and barely able to close. She felt herself floating among clouds, her body no longer under her own command.
She still remembered only that the person before her was the Emperor.
And she still remembered the words the Empress Dowager and Yuzhu had urged upon her.
To yield and to be willing.
Her fingers curled weakly into the Emperor's robe, and she gave a weak nod, unable to distinguish what was liking from what was willingness.
Wei Qi's body was taut, sweat beading at his brow, yet he held back and simply pulled the figure who had melted into water into his arms.
No matter how compliant and pliant the person in his arms was, he still caught a flicker of panic and unease in those half-lidded, blank eyes.
He did nothing more than kiss her. He had grown far more patient than before, and would not lose her again.
By the time the garments had fallen in a heap below the bed and the night had deepened, Xi Rongyan was long half-asleep, buried against Wei Qi's chest with her eyes unable to stay open.
Wei Qi tightened his grip on that soft waist. Looking at those sleeping features nestled so obediently in his arms, the expression in his eyes at last revealed his possessiveness, and he pulled the figure in his embrace ever closer.

chapters.title: Delight
chapters.content:
When Xi Rongyan woke the following morning, she felt the arm around her waist wound so tightly that she could barely breathe.
Just then, a languid and husky voice came from behind her: "Awake?"
Xi Rongyan went blank for a moment before quickly murmuring her assent. The fingers at her waist immediately tightened, and she was flipped over.
When she came back to herself, before her was a broad and powerful chest, laid bare before her without concealment.
It was her first time seeing a man's body so exposed. She stared blankly for a good while before, belatedly, she looked up — and met the Emperor's deep, watchful eyes.
Though those eyes betrayed no emotion, it seemed as though they contained a smile.
Yet even with that smile, the eyes beneath those sharp brows did not look particularly gentle.
Her cheeks felt a little hot. She propped herself up, intending to rise. "This concubine shall help Your Majesty dress."
Half of her hair had fallen over one of Xi Rongyan's shoulders. She supported herself with one hand beside him, those bright eyes looking at him, her face beneath the white gauze pure and delicately full, the collar of her garment gathered primly and carefully.
Wei Qi watched her. The fingers resting on her waist squeezed, then pressed her back down into his arms with slightly more force.
The fingers that had long gripped a sword bore a faint layer of callus — the sensation against Xi Rongyan's smooth skin was impossible to ignore.
He kneaded her fair earlobe next, his gaze fixed steadily on Xi Rongyan's eyes, still tinged with an innocent bewilderment, as he savored the feeling of her soft body nestled against him.
This was the first time the two of them had shared such lingering tenderness.
She had not resisted him.
What he had long yearned for — now that he had it, so this was what it felt like.
He only wished this moment could last a little longer.
He rested his hand on her back and let his fingers drink in the warmth of her body, then asked softly: "Did you sleep well last night?"
When the Emperor brought up last night, Xi Rongyan could not help but recall the scene of being kissed by him.
She had been so thoroughly dazed by the kissing that she had no memory of how she had even fallen asleep.
Her cheeks grew hot again. She bit her lip and dared not look the Emperor in the eyes. She lowered her gaze — only to be met with his bare chest.
The warmth rising from that chest left her flustered, and feeling even more bashful, she did not dare let her mind wander further. She gave a soft, quick nod.
The crimson corner of her lips caught between those small white teeth, leaving a faint, shallow red mark. Wei Qi's throat involuntarily bobbed. He knew how soft those lips were.
His gaze darkened a shade, and the fingers wrapped around her tightened.
It was precisely then that Gao Yi's prompting voice came from outside. Wei Qi drew a deep breath, and only leaned down to press his lips briefly to her forehead before releasing her and rising from the bed.
He watched Xi Rongyan prop herself up to rise along with him. He bent down and pressed a hand to her shoulder. "You may sleep a while longer."
With that, he went around behind the screen to let the palace attendants outside come in and help him dress.
Xi Rongyan was still sitting on the bed, staring blankly at the silhouette dressing beyond the screen. It then occurred to her that she ought to go and help.
She quickly rose and went out.
Seeing Xi Rongyan come over, and then seeing her slight frame in those thin garments — pale and still in the lamplight — Wei Qi extended his arm and pulled her into his embrace, pressing his lips to the top of her head with a quiet sigh.
He had succumbed to his longing for the smell of her. When she stepped forward, his heart had surged with a happiness he had not foreseen.
He had longed for her to come to him of her own accord.
The Xi Rongyan of the past had never once come to him of her own free will.
The outer robe was nearly fully dressed. A palace maid beside them held a tray bearing the jade pendant and sachet that Wei Qi wore. Xi Rongyan took them and meant to kneel to fasten them to the Emperor.
Her body was still held fast by the Emperor, who looked down at her. "Just fasten them for me like this."
Xi Rongyan looked into the Emperor's gentle eyes. In the warm lamplight, the Emperor's sharp edges were softened, and those keen brows and eyes grew tender. So the Emperor really was this gentle in private.
Her heart skipped a beat. She bent at the waist to carefully fasten the jade ornament for the Emperor.
The intermittent touch at his waist made Wei Qi's body go taut once more. He had restrained himself all last night, and now to see her actively fastening his jade pendant, seeing the faint red marks he had left upon her fair neck — he felt himself suddenly like one who had just discovered desire for the first time.
His fingers could not help but fall upon her bowed face — the true, soft sensation of her beneath his touch made him slowly release a breath.
Gao Yi, waiting outside, had never seen the Emperor linger so long in any consort's chambers. Even when he stayed in the Empress's palace, it had never been this long.
And then he heard the call for water, which startled him further.
The Emperor never stayed in a consort's chambers to wash and groom himself. Even when he spent the night, he was always fully dressed and gone by early morning.
While it was true the Emperor rarely spent nights in the inner palace, this time Gao Yi was genuinely taken aback — and he became even more certain that Consort Xi must not be taken lightly.
Inside the chamber, Wei Qi did not let Xi Rongyan see him out. On the contrary, when he saw the flush on her cheeks and noted that her eyes held a little less fear of him, he turned and left with a faint smile at his lips.
Seeing that smile on Wei Qi's face, Gao Yi felt as though he had seen a ghost.
In all his years waiting upon the Emperor, he could count on one hand the number of times he had seen him smile.
The moment the Emperor left, Yuzhu and Baozhu hurried inside.
Seeing Xi Rongyan still sitting dazedly on the bed, Yuzhu broke into a pleased smile. "This servant knew our mistress could do it."
Xi Rongyan was at a loss for words. Still somewhat muddled, she collapsed back onto the bed, clutching the brocade quilt, feeling pleasantly lazy. She looked up at Baozhu's face and, seeing that the red marks there had faded somewhat, she finally closed her eyes with some relief.
Seeing Xi Rongyan looking so languid, Yuzhu came forward and gently asked: "Mistress, last night did you..."
Xi Rongyan buried her face deeper into the quilt. Knowing what Yuzhu was asking, she felt the tips of her ears flame, and said quietly: "No..."
Yuzhu could not quite make out what Xi Rongyan meant. She spent a short while coaxing her before Xi Rongyan was finally persuaded to get up, wash, and dress.
When Baozhu tidied the bed, she turned it inside and out for a long while without finding what she expected to find. She stood puzzled for some time before running out and asking with some hesitation: "Mistress, the bed..."
Xi Rongyan understood what Baozhu meant. She turned to look at her and said, with relative calm: "The Emperor did not touch me last night."
Both Yuzhu and Baozhu were taken aback.
Yuzhu's expression shifted. Through the bed curtains earlier, she had still glimpsed the Emperor holding their mistress in his arms for quite a while that morning — it had not looked like she had failed to please him.
Xi Rongyan herself did not know how to explain it. She thought of the words the Emperor had said to her last night — had he noticed her fear and been considerate of her because of it?
In truth, last night she had been somewhat afraid, but she had made her preparations all the same. The Emperor's exceptional gentleness, however, had been beyond her expectations.
Yuzhu looked at Xi Rongyan's lost expression, and then her gaze fell to the faint red marks on Xi Rongyan's fair neck — clearly the work of a man's lips. She could not fathom it — they had clearly gone so far, so why had it not reached the final step?
Still, she did not have the heart to say anything. She knew their mistress, though reserved, understood the situation clearly and had her own sense of measure.
She called Baozhu to bring the face powder and helped Xi Rongyan conceal the red marks on her neck.

chapters.title: A Night of Hard Work
chapters.content:
When she had tidied herself and arrived at Yongchun Palace, the moment Xi Rongyan stepped inside she could feel the gaze of everyone there fall upon her.
She swept a glance over those looks — they were not particularly friendly.
She ignored them without so much as a flicker of expression and stepped forward to pay her respects to the Empress with proper decorum.
Song Helan sat in the seat of honor, her bearing elegant and dignified, her expression as she regarded Xi Rongyan difficult to read.
She had heard of Xi Rongyan before — the Empress Dowager's own niece, always summoned to the palace, with an excellent reputation among the daughters of noble families.
She had seen her before too: a beauty among ten thousand, the kind that made one envious and drawn to her at the same time.
Her two previous engagements had both been excellent matches, though both had ended in misfortune.
The Empress cast her eyes down, regarding the woman bowing before her — modest and unadorned.
She wore a robe the color of apricot blossoms and gossamer silk, the collar embroidered with blue cloud patterns, the sleeves wide and flowered, with a slender and graceful waist. In her dark hair, she wore only two silver-and-jade pins in the shape of magnolia flowers, which stood out beautifully against the black.
And her face was fair as a pear blossom, her downcast eyes like rolling pear clouds — quietly composed, with impeccable manners, without the slightest trace of restlessness or pride.
On the contrary, those naturally elegant brows like misty rain, those apricot-blossom eyes, those vermillion lips dotted by a small cherry — her voice was clear and melodious, and her appearance was one of gentle delicacy, the kind most likely to draw a man's tender care.
She was something like what she had imagined Xi Rongyan to be, yet in many ways different.
She understood now. The balance of the inner palace, maintained for so many years, could no longer hold.
Yesterday's events had been the Emperor's warning to her: whoever laid a hand on Xi Rongyan would find no quarter.
Yesterday afternoon she had gone to see the Emperor, and he had refused to see her even once — his customary coldness toward her, so cold that only the title of Empress gave her the smallest comfort.
A dignified smile rose to Song Helan's lips. In a gentle and measured voice, she addressed Xi Rongyan: "Consort Zhen, you must be tired after serving the Emperor through the night. You may rise."
She then had the head attendant offer Xi Rongyan a seat — arranged right at the very front.
Such a seating arrangement drew the gaze of everyone in the room back to Xi Rongyan once more.
All one could see was that composed and graceful figure, holding a lotus-pattern fan and resting it properly on her knees, sitting with perfectly straight posture, a string of white jade beads around her neck echoing the jade drops at her ears. Anyone who looked had to look twice.
Her fair, tranquil manner, elegant and clearly well-bred — like a fairy above the mortal world's smoke — only made everyone around her seem like the mud of the mundane.
The Empress watched the others' eyes and then addressed Xi Rongyan quietly: "Yesterday, Noble Consort Xian offended you. I hope you will not hold it against her."
"Let that matter pass."
A ripple of surprise went through the room.
They had all heard about yesterday's incident — word was that on the road, Noble Consort Xian had run into Xi Rongyan, and Xi Rongyan had simply ignored the Noble Consort. Relying on the Empress Dowager's backing, she seemed to look down on everyone. In the end, the two had a confrontation, and the Emperor actually took Xi Rongyan's side outright.
But why?
By the rules, it was Xi Rongyan who had been discourteous first. Why was the Noble Consort the one being punished?
Noble Consort Xian had the Empress behind her — was this Xi Rongyan truly so heedless of everyone?
First ignoring the Empress, and now ignoring the Noble Consort?
They whispered among themselves, all feeling something was off. But today the Noble Consort was not present, and then the Empress herself had spoken this way — it seemed the rumors were true.
And then they thought of how the Emperor had actually spent the entire night at Hanyuan Hall, and an involuntary envy rose in them. The gaze they directed at Xi Rongyan gained another layer of probing scrutiny and resentment.
They thought: she pretends to be unassuming and aloof from the world, but inside she is nothing but a fox spirit who knows how to perform innocence and win sympathy.
Xi Rongyan naturally felt those unfriendly eyes on her. The Empress's words had without doubt pushed her to the cresting wave. Those words were plainly biased in favor of Noble Consort Xian.
She had already grasped the Empress's attitude toward her. She steadied her heart, rose, and addressed the Empress respectfully: "Yesterday's incident came about because of a misunderstanding between this concubine and Noble Consort Xian."
"Yesterday the Empress Dowager summoned this concubine, and had someone inform Your Highness the Empress as well. Before Noble Consort Xian could hear this concubine's explanation, she struck me. In truth, this concubine has not harbored any resentment over it, and it has already been explained to His Majesty. As far as this concubine is concerned, the matter is settled and will not be dwelt upon."
In truth, Xi Rongyan had no wish to stir up trouble. Her intention had been to come today and, in the Empress's presence, clear up the matter with Noble Consort Xian so that the incident could be put to rest.
