She had gone to see the Empress Dowager first, but that did not mean she had been disrespectful to the Empress — the Empress Dowager had summoned her first, and the Empress had no grounds to fault her for it.
But just now she had looked around and not seen the Noble Consort; and then she heard the Empress bring it up on her own initiative. Knowing the relationship between the Empress and the Noble Consort, she understood that this needed to be addressed — for the others to hear it as well.
Song Helan looked at Xi Rongyan. A faint, cold smile curved her lips imperceptibly.
She appeared gentle and quiet, yet her tongue was sharp enough when it suited her.
She was evidently not the kind of person her surface manner suggested.
Yesterday's punishment of Noble Consort Xian had been so severe over such a small matter — it was impossible to believe Xi Rongyan had not stirred the pot and goaded the Emperor into it.
Song Helan let her gaze cool, and said softly: "You needn't speak of misunderstandings. Since the Emperor has taken your side, then the Noble Consort was in the wrong."
"The Emperor has already punished the Noble Consort. I mention this matter only to tell you that harmony in the inner palace is what matters most."
Song Helan wore an unreadable, faint smile. "Those petty misunderstandings and quarrels — bring them to me privately to be settled. There is no need to let things escalate."
"Don't you agree?"
"The Emperor favors you now. The others in the palace will naturally be happy for you and will not vie with you for anything. You, too, should be at peace."
No matter how one listened, there was another meaning beneath these words.
It was as though Xi Rongyan had deliberately stirred up trouble to flaunt her favor — or to show off the Emperor's affection.
Moreover, it was only now that Xi Rongyan learned the Noble Consort had been punished by the Emperor.
She noted how the others' expressions shifted after the Empress finished speaking — they had clearly been drawn in by those words. She was inwardly sorting through her response and about to speak when the Empress cut her off: "Consort Zhen, sit down for now. I have something to announce."
The Empress smiled. "This morning, Chief Eunuch Gao came to say that effective today, Consort Zhen's rank has been elevated to Noble Consort. The Emperor has personally granted her the title 'Zhen,' so she shall henceforth be known as Noble Consort Zhen."
"In your forms of address going forward, do not forget."
The others in the hall exchanged glances, their expressions startled as they looked toward Xi Rongyan.
A single night's stay, and she was immediately elevated in rank.
Entering the palace as a Zhaoyi consort was already exceptional enough. Now to be made a Noble Consort — in a few more days, might she not be raised to the rank of an Imperial Consort?
Word had it that Noble Consort Xian had her title stripped... and there was now a vacancy among the Four Noble Consorts...
Wang Xiuyi watched this scene, then let her eyes fall on Xi Rongyan's poised and proper bearing, and a complex expression crossed her face.
The person beside her gave her a nudge, smiling with an edge: "Come to think of it, the one who used to be most favored in the inner palace was you, sister. You've been here three years, and with all that favor, you're still only a Xiuyi consort."
"Here she's been a day, the Emperor spent just the one night, and her rank is already higher than yours."
"It truly is a matter of fate."
"Don't you think, sister?"
Wang Xiuyi's expression stiffened. She glanced at the person beside her, then clenched her hands tighter.
Xi Rongyan could naturally hear the murmuring, but her face remained utterly impassive.
She could tell that the Empress had been trying to position her as a common target.
Then someone spoke up with a smile: "Sister Zhen certainly has good fortune. Her childhood sweetheart and intended had barely died, and so quickly she has the Emperor's favor. Which of us sisters is as lucky as Consort Zhen?"
Xi Rongyan paused. Her fingers tightened.
A cold laugh came from below: "Indeed — and she's already brought two of them to their end. If she hadn't entered the palace, word is she couldn't even have gotten a marriage proposal."
"Look at Consort Zhen, not the least bit grieving. Turns out she had her eye on the Emperor."
That voice laughingly addressed Xi Rongyan: "Before, Sister Zhen came into the palace so often to see the Empress Dowager — was she perhaps often seeing the Emperor as well?"
Laughter rippled beneath the surface, hushed but clearly audible to Xi Rongyan: "She was awfully diligent about entering the palace — who knows what she was plotting?"
"That young Master Gu was so noble and treated her so well — who'd have thought she wasn't satisfied."

chapters.title: He Treated Her Differently
chapters.content:
The fingers Xi Rongyan had wrapped around her fan handle went white. She looked toward the one who had spoken.
A palace maid had quickly leaned in and whispered a name in Xi Rongyan's ear.
The speaker was Imperial Consort Qi, Lu Rongyue.
Imperial Consort Qi's eyes held a smile. She was not a particularly beautiful woman, but she gave off an impression of composure — yet the words she chose told a different story.
Xi Rongyan studied her carefully, her brows drawing together slightly. "I came to the palace in the past to keep the Empress Dowager company. Nothing more."
"I have no wish to speak of what is past. But to judge someone without knowing the full story — in that case, may I not make things up about you as well, sister?"
Lu Rongyue let out a cold snort and was about to reply when the Empress above suddenly frowned and cut in: "My intention was for all of you to get along with one another. Why has it come to this?"
"It is a good thing that Consort Zhen enjoys the Emperor's favor, and may she soon give the Emperor an heir and bring us good tidings."
"Let none of this be spoken of again."
With that, the Empress looked at Xi Rongyan: "If anyone in the future violates palace rules and offends you, you need not take it to the Emperor. Bring it to me, and I will deal with it."
She then cast a cold glance over the others: "Noble Consort Xian has already been stripped of her title by the Emperor and confined to Yanqiu Palace. Have you still not learned your lesson?"
The Empress's words seemed on the surface to speak on Xi Rongyan's behalf, but beneath them lay the implication that Xi Rongyan had been manipulating the Emperor with her favored position, using it to suppress the other consorts.
Xi Rongyan now understood everything in her heart. The Empress was not at all the magnanimous and fair-minded person she was reputed to be outside these walls. Born with a compassionate and gracious face, composed in her bearing, she had nevertheless managed to turn the entire room against her.
Letting others believe that yesterday's punishment of Noble Consort Xian had all been stirred up and instigated by her.
Sure enough, once the Empress's words settled, those unfriendly eyes grew even more unfriendly.
Imperial Consort Qi, Lu Rongyue, gave another soft snort: "Seeing as she has the Emperor's favor now, you'd all better watch yourselves. One wrong step in front of Consort Zhen, and she'll say something to the Emperor and have you sent to the cold palace."
"She's been here only a day, mind you. Tsk, tsk. Goodness knows what's coming next."
That yin-yang sarcasm made Xi Rongyan's heart sink. She rose and faced the room: "As for yesterday's matter: first, I did nothing improper; second, I did not start the conflict; third, however the Emperor chose to punish, I had no hand in it."
"Just now, Her Highness the Empress also said I was without fault in yesterday's matter. If you believe I entered the palace only to manipulate the Emperor into taking my side, think poorly of my character if you wish — but does that not also mean you think poorly of the Emperor? That he is someone who cannot distinguish right from wrong, and takes sides at whim?"
Xi Rongyan's voice was not loud, but every word was clear, delivered in a gentle and pleasant tone. The bearing of a well-bred noble lady — poised and gracious — left the others speechless for a moment.
No one dared to say another word. Who would dare speak ill of the Emperor?
Lu Rongyue shot Xi Rongyan a glance, clenching her fingers tight and grinding her teeth, but said nothing — giving only a cold hmph and looking away.
She had not expected Xi Rongyan to dare speak so openly.
Song Helan watched this scene, pressed her lips together, and dismissed the others, leaving only Xi Rongyan behind.
Song Helan was very courteous to Xi Rongyan, guiding her into the inner chamber and having her sit on the couch beside her.
A palace maid came to pour tea. Song Helan held her white cat elegantly in her arms, calmly watching Xi Rongyan sitting properly beside her.
The daughters of scholarly civil officials and the daughters of military officers were indeed somewhat different.
Reserved. Graceful.
Every gesture bespoke propriety and cultivation. The eyes moved softly, and in a single glance there was something almost poetic.
Most of the consorts in the inner palace now were women the Emperor had taken when he was still a prince — many of them daughters of military officers. All four imperial consorts and those of rank had been concubines and side-consorts from the prince's estate.
In the three years since the Emperor's ascension, selections had been held in the first year by court protocol — only three or four women chosen. The second year saw just two, casually appointed. This year, not even one had been brought in.
It was not that there were no women like Xi Rongyan in the inner palace, but today the Empress had seen it for herself — there was something distinctly different about her bearing.
No wonder the Emperor treated her differently. And as for her appearance — there were not two women in this entire inner palace who could match it.
Thinking of how the Emperor had confined her own cousin to house arrest, stripped her of her stipend and all the privileges of her title — all over Xi Rongyan — the Empress's eyes narrowed.
Xi Rongyan happened to turn her head and catch the Empress's expression. On that usually gentle face, there was a flash of something raw. The teacup in her hands trembled. She quietly lowered her eyes and drank her tea.
Song Helan watched Xi Rongyan's bowed profile and let her expression settle. She sighed quietly: "Yesterday's matter was indeed Noble Consort Xian's fault. Do not continue to blame her."
Xi Rongyan responded with proper decorum, shaking her head: "This concubine has never blamed the Noble Consort."
"I consider the matter past already."
Song Helan looked at Xi Rongyan, a note of regret in her eyes. "I have known Noble Consort Xian since childhood. Her character is somewhat pampered and willful — she speaks her mind and cannot conceal what she feels. After entering the palace, I had counseled her to mind her words and actions, but she never quite took my advice to heart."
She then reached out and took Xi Rongyan's hand: "She has always been impulsive, without a check on her tongue. Yesterday must have been frightening for you?"
Song Ningyu's rank was higher than Xi Rongyan's, and she was the Empress's own cousin. With the Empress framing it this way, Xi Rongyan naturally could not follow that line of thought.
She was well aware, too, that in the inner palace — where all were women — keeping a low profile was essential.
She made a genuine and quiet reply: "This concubine entered the palace hoping to live in harmony with the other sisters and serve the Emperor well. There was indeed a misunderstanding yesterday, but this concubine holds no blame toward Noble Consort Xian."
"Whatever His Majesty decided, this concubine had no part in it."
As she spoke, Xi Rongyan rose and bowed in apology to the Empress: "As for this concubine's failure to present herself to Your Highness the Empress first yesterday — the Empress Dowager's summons was urgent. This has weighed on this concubine's conscience, and I beg Your Highness's forgiveness."
Song Helan raised a brow and studied Xi Rongyan's obedient posture — fine brows, bright eyes, cherry lips, fair as snow. Every ornament on her person was precisely chosen: not overly plain, yet all in perfect complement to one another.
Her words were both humble and dignified.
One could see the depth that came with being a true noble family's daughter.
The Empress Dowager's niece — if she had been pampered and arrogant, she would have been easy to manage.
With this temperament, she still could not see through her.
Had she entered the palace willingly, or had something else brought her here?
That day, the Emperor had left without informing anyone and gone to the Flower Viewing Festival. It was also on that day that the Emperor issued the decree to bring Xi Rongyan into the palace.
The Empress had spent the last two days carefully recalling many past details. Xi Rongyan and the Emperor had truly had very few encounters before this.
Cining Palace, where the Empress Dowager resided, was far from the consorts' quarters. Xi Rongyan had most often come in the mornings, and the Emperor was almost always at Qinzheng Hall at that hour. The two of them rarely had opportunities to cross paths.
The one time they truly had met — as she had gathered — was when the Emperor had run into Xi Rongyan on the way to visit the Empress Dowager, and he had punished two palace maids because of her that very day.
Could it be that Xi Rongyan had already cast some kind of spell on the Emperor then?
Song Helan looked at Xi Rongyan steadily, suspecting that what lay behind all of this was the Empress Dowager's arrangement.
Even though the Emperor had only one prince, and the Emperor had still not named a crown prince, the Empress Dowager had begun to scheme.
A beauty trailing gossip and scandal, unfit to be arranged into any ordinary marriage — it was the perfect kind to be placed in the palace.
As a woman herself, Song Helan had to admit that Xi Rongyan was indeed the type to attract men. The Empress Dowager had truly played a fine hand.
Song Helan's eyes grew serious. But she took Xi Rongyan's hand warmly and said softly: "You needn't apologize. Both the Empress Dowager and the Emperor had someone come to explain. I did not fault you for it."
She had Xi Rongyan sit again, then addressed her: "Since you say yesterday's matter was a misunderstanding, and the Noble Consort herself knows she acted impulsively — what is needed now is for you to put in a word for the Noble Consort in front of the Emperor. We are all here to serve the Emperor, and harmony is what matters most."
"Rivalries and jealousies — are they really necessary?"
Xi Rongyan understood. Whatever she said right now in the Empress's presence, she had to comply.
In truth, she genuinely had no desire to stir up notice. Whether others believed her or not, she sincerely wanted peace and quiet.
But she was also unwilling to simply be a target for anyone's whims.
Xi Rongyan's expression remained respectful throughout. She said quietly: "When this concubine entered the palace, it was with the wish to live in harmony with the other sisters. This concubine is also sorry that such a thing occurred."
"If this concubine has the opportunity to see the Emperor again, she will plead on behalf of the Noble Consort."
She then looked toward the Empress. "But what His Majesty decides, this concubine dares not presume to influence. I can only do my best."
Song Helan smiled: "This matter arose because of you, so it is only fitting that you be the one to resolve it."
"Do not be so modest."
Though the Empress's face was perpetually wreathed in a gentle smile, it gave Xi Rongyan, for no apparent reason, a chill.
When she finally left Yongchun Palace, the brilliant light of a spring day fell upon her. Wherever she looked, there were only high walls — the horizon nowhere to be seen.

chapters.title: Delicate Beauty
chapters.content:
Walking the path back, she could not name what she felt.
She had thought of much: the looks the consorts had given her at the Empress's palace today, the mocking and cutting things they had said. Those words did not hurt her heart — but they had mentioned Yunyu-gege.
They had used Yunyu-gege to mock her, to strike at her most tender place.
Not even the dead could be left in peace. Now she had been dragged out to be ridiculed.
Yuzhu sensed something was wrong with Xi Rongyan. Seeing her walking with her head bowed, not saying a word, she quickened her steps to look at her face — and saw that Xi Rongyan's eyes had turned faintly red.
Of course they had. The Empress's seemingly gentle words had hidden barbs within them.
Though their mistress had responded beautifully today, having been cold-mocked by all those people still stung.
She said softly in comfort: "Mistress, don't think about those words. Once you have the standing to back yourself up, why would those words matter at all?"
Xi Rongyan glanced toward Yuzhu and said quietly: "I do not care about those words. I know those women said them to mock me deliberately."
She lifted her head to look at the palace walls and said, her voice a little rough: "Fighting and scheming is not what I wanted, yet I cannot escape it."
Yuzhu fell silent, looking at Xi Rongyan's eyes — bright and dark, clear in their distinction, carrying a note of sorrow.
She lightly dabbed at the faint moisture at the corner of Xi Rongyan's eyes with her handkerchief, and said softly: "Mistress, you are already inside the palace now. There is no going back."
"Did not the late Empress Dowager walk this same path in her time?"
"Without children, a consort is like a boat adrift at sea. The Empress Dowager cannot protect you for a lifetime."
Xi Rongyan said nothing, just walked forward silently.
When they were nearly at Hanyuan Hall, she suddenly heard a gentle call from ahead. She looked up, and there standing at the gate of her palace was her cousin, Xie Yumian, waiting for her.
The moment Xi Rongyan saw Xie Yumian, she pressed down the sorrow in her heart and quickened her steps toward her, a flicker of surprised pleasure on her face: "Sister, how long have you been waiting?"
Xie Yumian was Xi Rongyan's maternal cousin, two years her senior. They had been close friends since girlhood. Before Xi Rongyan entered the palace, she had often thought of coming to see her cousin when visiting the Empress Dowager, but had heard that the inner palace was strict — letters could not pass between them, and visits required a special imperial permit before family could be allowed in, with procedures so cumbersome it had seemed easier to let the idea go.
Xie Yumian gripped Xi Rongyan's hands tightly. Looking at Xi Rongyan's face — unchanged from the girl she remembered — she let out a quiet sigh.
She had never imagined Xi Rongyan would one day enter the palace.
She looked her up and down, then said softly: "Let us go inside and talk."
The two of them went in together.
The moment she stepped inside, Xie Yumian was greeted with an inner courtyard in full peach blossom bloom. Following Xi Rongyan's steps into the hall, she saw every corner had been thoughtfully and carefully arranged, and a feeling she could neither name nor fully understand began to stir in her.
She was still crammed into two rooms beside Imperial Consort Qi. Xi Rongyan had only just entered the palace, and already she was in the main hall.
She followed Xi Rongyan and sat on the wide couch. The clear morning light came in through the windows, filling the room with brightness.
Several times brighter than her own quarters.
She then looked at Xi Rongyan sitting beside her, already pouring tea for her with the same warm familiarity as before. She caught the scent — it was the Yuqun tea she had loved most during their girlhood days.
Back then, the two of them would tell each other everything, sitting by the large carved window on the spring couch, watching the rain fall outside, each holding a cup of Yuqun tea, sharing their deepest thoughts.
The steaming cup was extended toward her. Through the curling wisps of vapor, breathing in that familiar scent, she felt an odd, dreamlike disorientation — after so many years apart, meeting again like this, something felt subtly, painfully different.
She had not fared well in the palace.
Not even a fraction as well as Xi Rongyan, who had only just arrived.
Her fingertips closed around the cup, and she asked softly: "How do you have Yuqun tea here?"
Even tea in the palace was distributed by rank.
Those of the rank of Imperial Consort and above could request from the Internal Affairs Bureau whatever tea they wished. Those below that rank had no say in what was sent — the tea delivered to them was not theirs to choose.
And she was only an unf avored Cairen — the Internal Affairs Bureau paid no mind to what she received.
Xi Rongyan cradled her teacup and nestled close to Xie Yumian as she always had: "There are quite a few tea canisters on that side table — and as it happens, they are all teas I used to love."
"I knew you loved Yuqun tea, so I brewed it specifically. I had been hoping to invite you for a chat today."
Xie Yumian turned to look at her in quiet surprise, taking in those eyes of Xi Rongyan's — unchanged through the years, soft and warm like a spring rain, the kind that made you like her and want to be near her the moment you looked.
She had always been gentle and soft-spoken and kind. Xie Yumian had loved her best of all in their girlhood days.
Even as she watched her grow more and more beautiful right before her eyes, she had only felt glad for her — glad for that face, that nature, and reassured that she would have such a refined and elegant match as the young master of the Gu family.
She had truly been happy for her.
She had sincerely believed a woman like Xi Rongyan — as pure and luminous as white porcelain — deserved to be cherished and well-loved.
She had often looked after her in those years, and had hoped for her to live quietly and steadily.
Xie Yumian's eyes reddened. The memories of the past overwhelmed her with sudden pain. She set down her teacup and pulled Xi Rongyan tightly into her arms, breathing in the scent of peach blossoms on her, and said in a hoarse voice: "How did you end up in the palace?"
"Just now at the Empress's place, your sister did not speak up for you. Are you angry with me?"
Xi Rongyan understood the situation, had glimpsed some of the larger shape of things. She buried her head in Xie Yumian's shoulder, her eyes blurring with tears, and said softly: "I am not angry with you."
"I never intended to blame you."
Xie Yumian closed her eyes, and said again in that husky voice: "Almost everyone in the inner palace is on the Empress's side. The Emperor rarely favors anyone in the harem, and those of us selected later in the court drafts have no one to rely on here — we had no choice but to attach ourselves to her side."
"I have been placed in Yiqing Palace's Lanyue Hall, where Imperial Consort Qi resides. Just now I dared not speak up for you because I feared Imperial Consort Qi's retaliation."
"Please do not blame your sister."
Xi Rongyan shook her head: "I actually understand something of it. How could I blame you?"
Only then did Xie Yumian release Xi Rongyan, looking carefully at her face.
Seeing her reddened eyes, like peach blossoms fallen in water, a feeling she could not quite define rose in her heart once more.
She said: "I had heard about the Gu family's situation from within the palace. I was heartbroken for you, and yet powerless to help."
"I had prayed you would find another husband as fine as Young Master Gu."
"But I never imagined you'd somehow end up in the palace. Was it arranged by the Empress Dowager?"
Even now, Xi Rongyan felt as though her entry into the palace had all been a dream — something she could not clearly explain.
She shook her head: "It was not arranged by our aunt."
She lowered her gaze with a note of regret. "Our aunt had actually arranged another match for me. But by some twist of fate..."
"After Yunyu-gege's accident, my mother wanted to quickly find me another marriage. Going to the palace was never the intention."

chapters.title: And Yet You Came to the Palace
chapters.content:
Xie Yumian read Xi Rongyan's expression and could tell that she had not chosen to enter the palace.
She rested her hand on Xi Rongyan's fingers and was silent for a long while, unable to find the right words.
Gu Yunyu's accident had been so unexpected.
A noble young gentleman out for a pleasure trip, and those bandits had actually dared to rob him — one could only chalk it up to truly terrible luck, that he had happened to run straight into such desperate and violent criminals.
Xie Yumian shared her sorrow and said quietly: "The hearts of people in the inner palace are complicated. Especially now that you've also received the Emperor's favor."
"The only prince is the Empress's son, and General Song is the Emperor's trusted minister. The crown prince will sooner or later be the eldest prince."
"All we can do is depend on the Empress."
"And yet you came to the palace."
Xi Rongyan looked at Xie Yumian, a helpless smile on her lips. Seeing a familiar face at last brought some small comfort.
In truth, there was nothing more to say about entering the palace. The events of that day were best not revisited — to revisit them now would only bring more sorrow.
She looked down at the golden embroidered lotus on her fan and lost herself in thought for a moment. She simply said softly: "Since I am here, I can only take it one step at a time."
Xie Yumian nodded, then looked at Xi Rongyan's face and suddenly asked: "Is there only you living in this Guanju Palace?"
Xi Rongyan nodded.
Xie Yumian pressed her hands together, hesitated, and then spoke to Xi Rongyan: "Sister, you now have the Emperor's eye. May I ask something of you?"
Xi Rongyan looked at Xie Yumian. "What is it?"
Xie Yumian took Xi Rongyan's hand gently and said: "I would like to ask you to petition the Emperor to let me come and stay with you here in Guanju Palace."
"I see the side hall is empty, and you and I have been close since childhood. It would be good for us to keep each other company and talk."
Xi Rongyan hesitated a moment, then asked quietly: "I am still unfamiliar with the rules here in the palace. If I go over the Empress's head and ask the Emperor to move you here, would that be appropriate?"
Xie Yumian quickly assured her: "Don't worry, sister. As long as the Emperor gives the word, the Empress cannot object."
She gripped Xi Rongyan's hands tightly: "Sister, I truly want to come."
"We can support one another, keep each other company — it won't be so lonely."
Xie Yumian was indeed desperate to get away from Imperial Consort Qi.
In an ordinary month she could not see the Emperor even once.
From the time she had entered the palace until now, the Emperor had visited her quarters only once or twice — and had not even touched her on either occasion.
Imperial Consort Qi often belittled her with cutting words, and it was why the others also looked down on her.
Moreover, now that Xi Rongyan was in favor, she did not know how long that would last — but if she moved in alongside her, perhaps through Xi Rongyan she might manage to catch the Emperor's eye more often.
She was thoroughly exhausted by the cold loneliness of being out of favor.
Xi Rongyan knew that Xie Yumian was living in Imperial Consort Qi's quarters. Imperial Consort Qi was a mistress of her own palace, and she was close to the Empress.
Asking the Emperor to move her cousin here would inevitably offend both Imperial Consort Qi and the Empress.
But then she saw the faint redness around Xie Yumian's eyes as she pleaded — and realized she must be having a difficult time in Imperial Consort Qi's quarters to come to her with such a request.
As things stood, her relationship with the Empress was already somewhat strained. The question of offending her or not was moot.
She wavered only a moment before nodding. "Sister, do not worry. I will speak to the Emperor."
She paused, then looked at Xie Yumian. "But I have only just entered the palace and cannot yet gauge the Emperor's temperament. If he does not agree, please do not blame me."
Xie Yumian quickly nodded. "Sister, I understand. The Emperor is known for being cold and erratic — ordinary people do not dare get close to him."
"Even if it doesn't work out, I will not blame you."
Xi Rongyan gave a slight nod of relief. She said softly: "When the Emperor left this morning, he mentioned he would come back to dine with me. I will bring it up then."
She looked at Xie Yumian with a small smile. "If the Emperor agrees, we really would be able to be together often."
"But I can only do my best — I cannot promise anything. As long as you do not blame me, that is enough."
Xie Yumian heard Xi Rongyan's words and was startled into a brief silence.
She had been in the palace two years and had never heard of the Emperor dining with any of his consorts.
The Emperor rarely even spent the night in the inner palace, let alone shared a meal.
If the Emperor stayed in the inner palace more often, the succession would not be so sparse.
With so many women here, and yet only one prince and one princess between them.
She looked into Xi Rongyan's eyes. There were things she wanted to say, but could not quite bring herself to say them.
She gave a quiet nod and said lightly: "Of course not. If the Emperor does not agree, let it go. Just do not anger the Emperor on my account."
"The Emperor's visits are a good thing for you, sister. You must hold on to this opportunity."
Xi Rongyan's mind was full of thoughts at her cousin's words, but in the end she only nodded gently. "Thank you for telling me all this, sister. I will keep it in mind."
The two of them talked until close to noon, and Xi Rongyan casually invited Xie Yumian to stay and eat.
But Xie Yumian had to leave. The palace rules were strict — even between close friends among the consorts, a visit could not run too long, and sharing a meal together was not permitted.
When the hour came, she had to return.
Imperial Consort Qi kept a constant eye out for her mistakes. She was not on the Empress's side, and the Emperor rarely involved himself in inner palace affairs. The Empress held the highest authority here, and dealing with her was the simplest thing in the world.
She said quietly: "Sister and I will have many more chances to talk. Don't bother to walk me out — I'll find my own way."
With that she rose, not letting Xi Rongyan see her off, and walked out on her own.
Outside, she turned to look once more at the peach blossoms within the courtyard. A tide of thoughts surged within her, and she felt, unexpectedly, a small pang of envy.
She and Xi Rongyan had the same family background, had been close since childhood. She had never thought about it before — but now it seemed Xi Rongyan had everything going for her.
Back when the Gu family had their misfortune, she had grieved alongside Xi Rongyan.
Looking at it now, perhaps the one who needed sympathy was herself.
She wrapped her sleeves closer and walked ahead. Halfway along the path, she lifted her head — and saw, some distance ahead, a palanquin followed by more than a dozen eunuchs.
The man on the palanquin was noble and cold. She stood still and bowed to one side, and he did not spare her so much as a glance.
It was as though she were no different from one of the plain, unremarkable bricks on the palace wall.
Until the palanquin had passed by her side. She turned to watch it — and saw it stop at the gate of Hanyuan Hall.
The Emperor descended from the palanquin and strode inside.
She looked up at the sky. The brilliant light of the spring day stung her eyes. She blinked, and a bitter feeling arose of its own accord.
She understood once again, in that moment, the envious eyes those consorts had worn at the Empress's palace today.
Because she was envious too.

chapters.title: Yan'er, Don't Be Afraid
chapters.content:
After Xie Yumian left, Xi Rongyan rose and went to sit on the spring couch behind the screen, lost in thought.
Seeing her old cousin again, remembering so many things from their girlhood days together, left her with a hollow, drifting feeling.
Baozhu came in from outside with two peach blossom sprigs and offered them up as comfort: "Mistress, stop letting your mind wander. Those people can say what they like — they are only jealous of you."
Xi Rongyan looked at the peach blossoms placed before her and took one sprig in her hand. She stared at it in a daze for a moment, then rested her cheek on her hand and said softly: "After spring passes, the peach blossoms will fall."
"And the begonia blossoms will fall too."
"Then the lotus and the roses will bloom — a profusion of flowers competing for beauty. There will be more than enough for their envy."
Baozhu softly agreed, then added: "But the peach blossoms and begonias will bloom again next year. Why should mistress worry so much?"
Xi Rongyan was quiet for a moment, then plucked a peach petal and let it fall onto the carpet. She spoke in a low voice: "I only feel this way because I saw my cousin today and was reminded of the past — I cannot calm myself just yet."
"She used to be a bright and laughing woman. Today when I saw her, her face was full of sadness, and even her smiles seemed forced."
"I only hope I can truly help her and give her some comfort."
Halfway through her words, Xi Rongyan paused.
She had only just entered the palace, and she herself did not know how long the Emperor's favor would last, or whether she was even of any consequence in this inner palace.
Just then, the voice of a palace maid came from outside, announcing the Emperor's arrival.
Xi Rongyan startled, and before she could even properly rise from the spring couch, the Emperor had already stepped through the screen.
She hastily scrambled to her feet to perform the court bow.
But she had barely begun to bend at the waist before something tightened at her waist. When she came back to herself, she was already sitting in the Emperor's lap.
She felt a slight unease at such closeness — she was still not accustomed to this kind of proximity.
The Emperor's breath fell at her collar, warm and a little suffocating.
Wei Qi looked down at Xi Rongyan's fair profile. Back then, she had never once sat so quietly in his arms.
Though she was soft and timid, when she lost her temper she could be quite troublesome — biting and scratching. He had been afraid of hurting her with his strength and had held back, and though he'd grown angry, it was always him who relented in the end.
Now this rare moment of closeness had his heart going soft. Seeing the faint red rim at her eyes, his gaze darkened. He pulled her tightly against him, and his fingers caressed her eyelids as he asked, with genuine concern: "Did the Empress give you trouble?"
Xi Rongyan startled and looked up. The Emperor's eyes were full of care and tenderness.
The last time she had come to the palace to see the Emperor, he had seemed somewhat gentle — but there had been a depth to his eyes that had made her a little afraid.
Now, seeing nothing but concern in those eyes, her heart gave a small, inexplicable jump.
She also remembered how gently he had called her name last night while kissing her.
She was bewildered. Why did everyone say the Emperor was cold and cruel, and even her cousin had said so? If the Emperor treated only her this way, and yet she had truly had so very few interactions with him...
She hesitated, and simply shook her head.
Wei Qi saw Xi Rongyan's lost expression and silently let his gaze deepen. He pulled her closer.
He patted her back lightly, saying nothing — and yet it felt like comfort.
Like gentle, warm sunlight, it left Xi Rongyan both startled and warmed somewhere deep inside.
In her hands she still held a peach sprig. Her fair, delicate fingers turned the petals idly. With the Emperor so unexpectedly gentle, she had a feeling of being caught in a dream.
Wei Qi looked down. Those full, soft lips were right before him.
He wanted to kiss her again.
But he was still afraid of frightening her.
In the past, Xi Rongyan feared him. The moment she saw him coming, she would hide. Every time he kissed her, he had to force her chin up hard to get her to open her mouth.
He knew he was hurting her with that grip, and he knew she was in pain — and yet she never learned, always forcing him to use more pressure.
Looking back now, those memories were painful ones for Wei Qi as well.
More than once he had envied that dead man.
He could only vent his frustration by tormenting her, and he had demanded of her countless times what that dead man had that he did not. Each time, she only answered with silence.
Her silence was more excruciating to him than if she had spoken.
Wei Qi's thoughts drifted inward. Without realizing it, the hand holding Xi Rongyan's tightened. When he came back to himself, Xi Rongyan was looking at him with an expression of alarm.
That look again.
His darkened expression shifted, and his gaze fell to the gilded lotus lamp column nearby, which cast a warped and blurred reflection of his own grim features.
He was startled for a moment, then quickly raised his hand to cover Xi Rongyan's eyes. He bent and rested his chin on her shoulder with its pale pink embroidered begonia, and said in a low, rough voice: "Yan'er. Don't be afraid."
He tightened his arms around her. "The situation in the north is pressing, and it weighs on me."
Xi Rongyan had truly been frightened by the Emperor's expression just then.
He already had something naturally fierce about his bearing, and when those eyes went dark, they were terrifying.
It was said that in the north, even chieftains of rival tribes had been stilled by the sight of the Emperor — those eyes, when narrowed, seemed to flash with the light of blood, like a savage beast about to kill.
This was the first time she had seen that look.
The man who had walked in just now and the one before her now seemed like two different people.
Now, with Wei Qi's palm over her eyes and his gentle words in her ear, her thoughts grew muddled.
She did not know there was trouble in the north. Perhaps it was truly that.
Still unnerved, her heart pounding, she nodded with great docility.
Wei Qi released his fingers, then leaned back slightly to look at the person in his arms. He lifted her chin and looked at those still-uncertain eyes, then bent down and pressed his lips gently to her eyelids.
He held her for a long while, knowing he had not controlled his emotions well and had frightened her again.
She had always said he looked frightening.
She had said she was accustomed to someone as warm and gentle as Gu Yunyu.
Wei Qi lifted his eyes again toward the lamp column. The shape it cast was twisted and distorted — as though he could never transform into the kind of person she loved.
His long fingers fell, one by one, into her hair. He closed his eyes and asked: "At the Empress's place this morning — was there anyone who showed you disrespect?"
Xi Rongyan was being held so tightly by the Emperor she could barely breathe, and then to have him suddenly ask this — she hesitated.
She shook her head again: "There was not."
Wei Qi pressed his lips together. He knew that asking Xi Rongyan directly would get him nowhere most of the time.
This nature of hers had not changed much.
In the previous life, even when Noble Consort Xian bullied her, she had never mentioned it in front of him.
He had put Noble Consort Xian in the cold palace preemptively, partly out of worry that this nature of hers would lead her to be wronged again.
Wei Qi did not press further. He only patted her back softly. "In a little while, I will raise your rank again, and then move you to Chengqian Palace."
"That place has been empty for some time and is being renovated. Bear with it a little longer."
"It is close to my Mingde Hall. Once you move there, we will live together, and you may come find me at Mingde Hall whenever you like. No one will dare do anything to you then — not even the Empress."
Xi Rongyan was stunned. She stared blankly at the dragon embroidery on the Emperor's dark robe and almost thought she had misheard.
Had those words truly been spoken to her?
To move her to Chengqian Palace — the palace closest to Mingde Hall — and to live there together with the Emperor.
However she heard it, it seemed impossible.
Just then the announcement of the meal came from outside. Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan, still dazed, and did not bother waiting for her response.
At least now he had the advantage. Slowly, he would manage to make a place for himself in her heart.
He took her hand and led her out. The palace maids came to serve the dishes, but Wei Qi waved them all away. He personally placed food in Xi Rongyan's bowl.
Xi Rongyan was momentarily overwhelmed, looking at the chopstick-load of vinegared conch delivered toward her lips, then at the Emperor's patient, smiling eyes. At last she parted her lips and took the chopsticks between her teeth.
Wei Qi watched those silver chopsticks disappear between those crimson lips, and smiled. He then picked up a piece of the little fragrant bamboo shoots.
These were all dishes Xi Rongyan loved. She had a fondness for sour and sweet flavors, and he had arranged it all for her so that entering the palace would never make her feel wronged.

chapters.title: I Will Come Dine With You Tonight
chapters.content:
From the moment that first chopstick-full had started things off, Xi Rongyan had barely had a chance to feed herself.
By the end, she had somehow found herself sitting on the Emperor's lap once more, being coaxed by him to eat a little more.
Xi Rongyan's cheeks were flushed crimson. Finally, truly unable to eat another bite, she lightly pushed at the Emperor's hand, her eyes tinged with a small plea: "Your Majesty, I truly cannot eat any more."
Wei Qi cast his eyes downward at Xi Rongyan, at the way she still seemed slightly careful and tentative. Though still reserved and proper, at least she was pliant.
Back then, to get her to eat even one bite from him had always taken until both of them were exhausted.
In truth, Wei Qi wanted Xi Rongyan to eat a little more — for the sake of her health — but he would not force her. He took the handkerchief from the maid beside them and personally wiped her mouth.
He asked: "Truly full?"
Xi Rongyan nodded quickly: "Truly."
Only then did Wei Qi feel reassured. He waited for her to rinse her mouth, then carried her in his arms toward the inner chamber and set her on the bed.
Xi Rongyan looked up with some bewilderment at Wei Qi standing before her, and her heart began to flutter anxiously again.
Wei Qi was tall, with broad shoulders, and when he bore down over her, the weight was crushing and fearsome.
Wei Qi read all of Xi Rongyan's thoughts. Xi Rongyan's mind was not difficult for him to guess.
He simply sat down beside her, and said to her in a low voice: "Spring makes one drowsy. You are tired — sleep for a while. When you wake, I will have someone bring you milk porridge."
Xi Rongyan was startled again.
Back in her family home, during spring she always took a small midday nap, and when she woke she found her mouth tasteless and liked to eat a bowl of milk porridge. It had been a habit of many years.
But how could this be such a coincidence?
She opened her lips, hesitating — wanting to ask but not knowing how.
Wei Qi smiled slightly: "I had someone go and inquire at your family home."
Though these words cleared up Xi Rongyan's confusion, they also astonished her that the Emperor had put so much thought into her — had specifically sent someone to find out her preferences.
No wonder the dishes at the table had all been things she liked.
Her body was gathered into a warm embrace, the strong heartbeat inside steady and sure. For the first time, she felt that perhaps the Emperor was not so frightening after all.
The Emperor's large palm gently stroked her back. His voice, warm as the light that filtered in through the window branches, was gentle: "You've grown a bit thin. I will come a little earlier tonight to dine with you."
Xi Rongyan breathed in the scent of dragon-ambergris incense at the tip of her nose, listened to the Emperor's gentle voice, and let it fill the blank spaces of her uncertainty. She closed her eyes and let out a quiet sound of assent.
Then she hesitated and cautiously looked up at the Emperor. She bit her lip, thought it over, and spoke: "Would Your Majesty allow this concubine's cousin to come and accompany her?"
"There is space beside Hanyuan Hall, and this concubine lives here alone. It would be good to have my cousin for company and conversation."
As she spoke, Xi Rongyan's fingers nonetheless tightened with nervousness. She truly had not yet figured out the Emperor's temperament and did not know how he would react.
Watching the Emperor's deep, downward gaze meet hers, her heart pounded with anxiety.
Even though she knew the Emperor had been very gentle and kind to her, she was still unsettled.
In truth, Wei Qi was not pleased at the idea of someone else living here.
He had a memory of Xi Rongyan's cousin. In the previous life, it was she who had helped Xi Rongyan escape — but it was also she who had revealed Xi Rongyan's whereabouts.
To earn favor and protect herself, she had easily betrayed Xi Rongyan.
If not for fearing Xi Rongyan would resent him for it, he would have dealt with her long ago.
But right now he also did not want to refuse Xi Rongyan.
Xi Rongyan had only just started to be a little less afraid of his closeness. If he refused, he worried she would be uneasy and imagine things.
Wei Qi thought it over inwardly, bent down, and caressed Xi Rongyan's face: "This matter is noted. Don't worry — I will make arrangements."
Xi Rongyan had not held out much hope, yet it sounded as though the Emperor had agreed.
Her eyes lit up. She rose immediately to express her gratitude.
Wei Qi saw the brightness in Xi Rongyan's eyes and concealed the complexity of his own feelings, letting his gaze drop to cover them.
Xi Rongyan was always happiest over things that concerned other people. In truth, she devoted very little thought to herself.
And in the past, she had never once truly looked at him.
He had no wish to let Xi Rongyan see his old grievances and resentments. In any case, all of that was past.
Everything could still be made right now.
He kneaded Xi Rongyan's smooth palm lightly, burying the possessive desire rising in him, and left.
When he stepped out, Wei Qi stopped for a moment. His brow darkened beneath the black robe, a cool edge returning to his expression. He mounted the imperial palanquin and went to the Empress's palace.
In Yongchun Palace, the Empress heard the words from the head attendant at her side and reached out in anger to grip a fistful of cat fur. At once a yowl rang out, and the cat squirmed and leapt from Song Helan's arms, scrabbling away.
Song Helan took a deep breath, smoothed the fur from her skirt, and leaned back against the soft cushions. She looked sidelong at the attendant and said with a cold smile: "Oh? The Emperor personally went over at noon to dine with her?"
Nanny Yu's heart was thudding under the Empress's gentle yet frigid gaze. She nodded: "Little Linzi came back and said the Emperor stayed quite a long while."
Song Helan's lips curved with a contemptuous smile.
In seven years of accompanying the Emperor, she could count on one hand the times they had shared a noon meal.
And Xi Rongyan had only just entered the palace, yet the Emperor was already this attentive.
Nanny Yu read the Empress's expression and leaned in quietly: "In truth, it would not be hard for you to deal with her."
She bent close and whispered something in Song Helan's ear.
Song Helan raised a brow, and smiled mildly: "Receiving a little favor is nothing. There is no need for me to make a move."
"Let us wait a few days and see whether the Emperor is simply drawn by novelty."
Nanny Yu thought this reasonable. The Emperor over all these years — she had watched from the Empress's side. It was not so much that the Emperor rarely favored the consorts, but that he had never truly loved any of them.
That Wang beauty before — how stunning, how alluring she was, easily a match for Consort Zhen — and the Emperor hadn't looked at her twice, had never even visited.
Perhaps this time it really was just the appeal of something new.
Just as they were discussing this, the curtain was swept aside from outside, and a palace woman hurried to the Empress's side, bending close and saying in a low voice: "Your Highness, the Emperor has come."
Song Helan was taken aback. The Emperor had not come in a very long time.
She suppressed the flicker of delight that crossed her face, keeping her expression composed and dignified, and rose quickly.
Meanwhile, back at Hanyuan Hall, once the Emperor had left, Xi Rongyan let herself sink into the bed. She and Yuzhu chatted idly.
She yawned — come spring, she always felt sleepy.
Yuzhu was still beside her, earnestly saying: "The Emperor is so attentive to mistress, even had someone go inquire about your preferences — does he not love you?"
"Mistress, you must seize this opportunity. Tonight, if you were to be a little more proactive..."
Before she could finish, Xi Rongyan suddenly pulled the quilt up over her head. The muffled voice that came from inside said: "Yuzhu. I understand."
These things Xi Rongyan understood perfectly. It was just the matter of being proactive in that way...
She truly did not know if she could manage it.
Yuzhu was at a loss, and had no choice but to tiptoe out.
Once Xi Rongyan heard that no one was beside her anymore, she gently lifted the quilt and stared up at the canopy above, lost in thought. Then she turned her head — and saw Baozhu sitting quietly and faithfully by her side.
The wound on Baozhu's face still bore a red mark. Xi Rongyan reached out and touched it gently. "Does it still hurt?"
Baozhu smiled and shook her head. "It doesn't hurt anymore."
Xi Rongyan said nothing. She pulled the quilt up around herself, turned over onto her other side.
After a long while, she lay there still, eyes open and restless.
She herself was anxious and unsettled.
She only knew that since she had entered the palace, she had to slowly start looking ahead.

chapters.title: You Want Me to Feed You?
chapters.content:
That afternoon, the moment the sky outside began to darken, Xi Rongyan's heart grew anxious.
The Emperor had said he would come and dine with her tonight, and now the dishes had all been laid out and were starting to cool.
She was a little hungry, in truth.
She was debating whether to start eating when the palace maid who had been keeping watch outside hurried in and announced joyfully: "Mistress, the Emperor has arrived."
Xi Rongyan could not tell whether she felt relief or something else. She rose to go out and receive him. Before she could even perform the court bow, the Emperor had already wrapped an arm around her shoulder and guided her inside.
The Emperor even offered a quiet explanation: "It was a little busy. I'm later than expected."
With that, she was taken by the Emperor's hand and led to sit beside him. Naturally and without ceremony, the Emperor took the damp cloth from the maid beside them and, while wiping Xi Rongyan's hands, asked: "Have you been waiting long? Are you hungry?"
Even as he asked it, Wei Qi knew the question was unnecessary — of course Xi Rongyan would shake her head.
Xi Rongyan looked down blankly at her own hands lying in the Emperor's palm, being wiped clean with such care and gentleness. The Emperor would actually wait on her like this.
He was being so good to her.
Even if the Emperor had come late, he need not have explained himself to her.
She looked up dazedly at the handsome, warm face before her. The palace lamp flickered, and for the first time she noticed the Emperor was also extraordinarily handsome.
The Emperor she saw in private was nothing like the one others described.
Wei Qi finished wiping her hands, placed a pair of silver chopsticks in hers, then asked what dishes she preferred. All of it was done with such warmth and ease, as though he had done it thousands of times before.
Only then did Xi Rongyan notice the table had been reset. She understood that when the Emperor arrived and learned he was late, he must have had fresh dishes prepared.
Again the table was covered with piping hot dishes of all her favorites. Under the Emperor's gaze, she reached down and took a piece of stir-fried almond, but then she could not help glancing sideways at the Emperor's face.
The Emperor was watching her with a warm and steady expression, as though the flash of something dark and twisted that had crossed his face at noon had been nothing but her imagination.
Another helping was added to her bowl, and the low, warm voice came at her ear: "Looking at me like that — do you want me to feed you?"
Xi Rongyan blinked. Her face blazed red. She quickly lowered her head.
Wei Qi silently tugged at the corner of his mouth, his gaze fixed at the edge of his vision entirely on her.
He thought again of that evening shortly after Gu Yunyu's death, when she had come to see him.
It had been a deep autumn night, the air bitterly cold outside. She had been wrapped in thick brocade robes, her eyes faintly red, the hollows beneath them dark with exhaustion, a white ribbon bound at her forehead. Though her dark hair was adorned only with a single silver pin, she had been, in his eyes at that moment, unutterably beautiful.
With just one gentle lowering of those eyes, his heart had surged and he had immediately wanted to possess this woman.
He could not say when he had first resolved that he must have her — perhaps it was each time he heard that she was coming into the palace to see the Empress Dowager, his heart pulling taut at the thought.
Picturing her slow approach and the serene, pale-clothed figure of her.
That day she had knelt before him and pleaded on behalf of the Gu family. Yet in his eyes, she had already become his.
He had invited her to a private dinner, and the table had been covered with things carefully chosen for her.
And a jug of lì huā chūn wine.
He had feared she would be frightened or too inhibited, and had prepared the wine especially for her.
It had been warmed, so it would not be cold when she drank it.
That night, alone at the table together, her face had been pale and trembling with fear — so restrained and careful, just as she was now. Not a single bite eaten properly.
But back then she had been more consumed by grief after a great loss, clinging only to the faintest thread of will for the sake of her child with Gu Yunyu.
He had treated her like prey, and had personally poured her wine.
But she had not drunk it. She was clever enough to sense something was wrong, and had knelt before him, pale and shaking.
Baring that fair, slender neck of hers — the most tender and soft part of herself — directly before a hunter's eyes.
What a shame.
He had prepared the wine for her with his own hands.
She could have drank it, let herself yield to the haze of wine, and let things happen. Instead, she had surprised him — she was more steadfast than he had anticipated.
That had not been an enjoyable evening.
Later, it became impossible to share a proper meal with her. She had never once cooperated.
Now, her cheeks faintly flushed, she sat quietly at his side. What she gave him was a feeling entirely different.
He knew himself — he preferred this.
As long as she did not think of leaving, that was enough.
After dinner, Wei Qi held Xi Rongyan against him on the small couch and read.
Xi Rongyan was enclosed in the Emperor's arms. The sound of turning pages was like the beating of her startled heart, and she shifted a little stiffly.
She was surrounded by the Emperor's presence, and did not know what to say. The Emperor did not seem to be the kind of person who made idle conversation.
Fortunately, the palace maid came in to announce that the water was ready, and she said, as though released: "This concubine will go bathe first."
Wei Qi's arms were wound around that slender waist. In truth he had no inclination to read — he simply wanted an excuse to hold her longer.
He did not know what to say to her, either. Even in the previous life, they had never truly spoken to each other.
He did not know how to please a woman.
Breathing in that sweet fragrance of hers, enduring it had been no easy matter for him either. Hearing that she was going to bathe, he felt his body tighten, and then he released her.
He very much wanted to go with her. But he knew how reserved she was, and in the end he restrained himself, thinking of letting things move at their own pace.
Once inside the bathing room, Xi Rongyan finally let out a long breath. Baozhu scrubbed her back for her, and murmured: "I was peeking at the Emperor just now — he really is so handsome. Did mistress notice?"
In truth, up to this point Xi Rongyan had not once dared to look the Emperor full in the face and study his features.
She knew he was exceptionally handsome. It was just that the killing air around him was too heavy.
This was the first time she had ever felt what a killing air was — when the Emperor was not smiling, he was genuinely impossible to approach. Perhaps that was why so many people said the Emperor was cold and ruthless.
Xi Rongyan rested her cheek on her hand. In the warmth of the steam, she murmured a vague reply, her eyes half-lidded, languid and unwilling to leave.
She was, in truth, quite nervous.
The hot water had been replenished several times over, and Baozhu could not help but say: "Mistress, you have been soaking for over half an hour."
Xi Rongyan knew she could not delay any longer, and finally rose.
When she came out, the Emperor was already sitting on the edge of the bed waiting for her. His deep, dark eyes fixed on Xi Rongyan the moment she appeared and did not leave her, and her heart went tight.
She moved in small steps toward Wei Qi.
Wei Qi watched Xi Rongyan's bashful manner. He liked seeing her bashful.
They said a woman was only bashful when she was drawn to someone. Now that Gu Yunyu was long dead — had she perhaps begun to have some place for him in her heart?
The still-damp strands of hair were still dripping water, the drops falling from her fair and slender neck downward.
Before him was her slender waist. He knew how soft it was.
Even though she was a married woman, she still carried about her a quality that made one want to pull her close and take hold of her.
Like a just-ripened apricot, tender and sweet, the kind one could not help but want to bite into.
Wei Qi suppressed his own impulse with considerable effort. He drew her into his arms and took the cloth from the palace maid's hands to dry her wet hair for her.
He had enough time and patience.
There would be no one else to come between them.
One day she would understand that he was better than Gu Yunyu in every way.
Whatever gentle care Gu Yunyu had given her, he could give her too.

chapters.title: A Nightmare
chapters.content:
Her delicate shoulders were stained with dark patches of wet.
Her soft, long hair was spread across her slight back, damp and curling.
She was obedient. She was compliant.
And she was clear as still water.
Wei Qi's gaze, behind Xi Rongyan where she could not see it, grew deeper and deeper. He had only to lift his eyes, and every palace maid in the inner chamber felt a chill in their bones — they bowed their heads and withdrew.
Yuzhu had been standing watch beside Xi Rongyan, but sensing a coolness in the air, she looked up and met Wei Qi's gaze. Frightened, she hesitated only a moment before lowering her head and retreating as well.
Xi Rongyan, slow to realize what had happened, found that all the palace servants had withdrawn. She was confused — why had even Yuzhu left?
Now there was only the two of them in the room. She grew tense again.
The feeling of her long hair being lifted and dried a little at a time by the Emperor sent a strange warmth through her. The Emperor would actually be willing to do such a thing for her.
He was, after all, an emperor above all others.
The gentle movements made her feel pleasantly drowsy. Even the tension began to ease.
The movements were so light. The oppressive quality she had once associated with the scent of dragon-ambergris incense on him — she had grown used to it, she realized.
The warmth of the man's chest drifted against her back at intervals. She closed her eyes contentedly. The back that had been held so rigidly straight gradually curled inward, slowly leaning into Wei Qi's embrace.
That soft body actually leaning toward him on its own — in the past, that had been nearly impossible.
Wei Qi's hands stilled. His palm settled on her shoulder, and he bent his head to look at her resting there on his shoulder without a trace of guard, seemingly asleep. His breath involuntarily deepened.
His body closed in of its own accord. His eyes rested only on the faintly parted lips before him.
She would also lean toward him on her own.
Wei Qi's throat bobbed. But he was careful, afraid to startle her. He slowly eased her down onto the bed.
But Xi Rongyan began to dream. She dreamt she was pinned beneath a tall man, the candlelight dim all around her, the heavy bed curtains pressing close on every side.
The only thing in her field of vision was the rise and fall of the man's broad chest, which bore a scar half-visible, half-hidden. She found it somehow familiar and reached out to touch it — but then she realized her wrists were pinned above her head by that man's hands, unable to move.
Fear crept in and overtook her heart. She became aware of a deep, layered pain on her body. She strained her neck upward to look at the man's face, and all she could see were a pair of eyes wild with desire.
Blood-red, like a ferocious beast about to devour her.
She cried out in fright, her voice trembling and choked. "Let me go..."
Wei Qi's brow furrowed. The person in his arms had pushed her hands against his chest, and her legs had begun to kick at him. Tears slid from the corners of her eyes.
In that instant, Wei Qi seemed to see the Xi Rongyan of the previous life. The moment he came near her, she would struggle.
Even in sleep, her body instinctively resisted his approach, did it?
Even now, when she had not married Gu Yunyu, she still loathed him just as much?
His expression grew gradually dark. The fingers braced beside her face slowly coiled, trembling faintly with the force of their grip.
The memories of the past surged forward. Wei Qi knew he was losing control of his emotions.
He wanted to wake her and demand of her — in what single way was he inferior to Gu Yunyu?
But just then Xi Rongyan suddenly woke, her tear-filled eyes blinking open.
The figure before her was blurred and indistinct. She could not make out his expression, only that a large silhouette loomed over her, and her heart leapt with instinctive fear.
She thought she was still dreaming. Her body moved sideways to escape — but then a large hand caught her shoulder, and she was pulled into a warm embrace.
The fingers on her back moved in gentle, soothing strokes. A low voice fell at her neck: "Yan'er. Was it a nightmare?"
That voice was familiar. There was a strong heartbeat at her ear, and the soft motion at her back slowly released the knot of tension inside her. She lifted her head, and through her blurred, tear-filled eyes she could just make out a pair of eyes gazing down at her with concern.
Tears slid from the corner of her eye down to her temple. She blinked, and the face before her grew gradually clear.
She looked at the person in front of her, and in that moment, a swell of grief rose in her. Her lips trembled. She turned her head and buried it in Wei Qi's chest, circling her arms around Wei Qi's waist and holding tight, her voice trembling: "I was frightened..."
Wei Qi gently stroked Xi Rongyan's soft hair in the dim lamplight, lips pressed close, patiently coaxing her until the figure in his arms gradually quieted.
Sinking in the Emperor's gentleness, she was no longer so afraid of him. She looked up again, and found the Emperor also looking down at her. The white robe at his shoulder had been pulled down in her clutching, and was left exposed.
It was still the third month, and the nights carried a faint chill.
The Emperor had held her and soothed her all this while. She did not know how long he had been holding her.
She only felt that the Emperor's embrace was, after all, so warm.
She bit her lip, lowered her head, and said in a very small voice: "Did this concubine offend Your Majesty just now?"
Wei Qi felt the fingers clutched in his robe tighten. He let out a quiet sigh and turned her in his arms so they both lay on their sides on the bed. His long fingers gently wiped the lingering traces of tears at the corner of her eyes. Looking at those reddened eyes, he spoke gently: "Did I frighten you?"
Xi Rongyan shook her head, lowered her gaze, and said quietly: "This concubine just had a nightmare."
Wei Qi wrapped an arm around Xi Rongyan's waist and pulled her closer against him. His voice was low, husky, and gently coaxing: "What sort of nightmare?"
Xi Rongyan's eyes were fixed on the exposed collarbone visible at the Emperor's collar. She parted her lips, wanting to speak, then thought better of it.
She could hardly say she had dreamt of being beneath a fierce and terrible stranger...
She did not tell the truth. Her voice came out very small: "This concubine dreamt she was being bitten by a tiger."
The words had no sooner left her mouth than there was a low laugh.
She startled and looked up — she saw the Emperor's smiling eyes, and then a warm breath rushed toward her.
The Emperor lowered his head and leaned in toward her. Her face blazed suddenly hot.
The Emperor's large hand cupped her face, and she heard the Emperor's low voice: "So Yan'er is afraid of tigers. From now on, I will be with Yan'er every night. If Yan'er is frightened, just hold on to me."
Xi Rongyan looked at the Emperor's eyes in a daze. Those gentle eyes left her in a moment of bewilderment.
Before she knew what she was doing, she had already let out a quiet murmur of assent.
Her forehead was touched lightly by the Emperor's lips. Her body was pulled firmly into the Emperor's arms, and from above her came the Emperor's sighing voice: "Yan'er is always so timid. In the future, Yan'er need only lean on me."
"I will never let anyone harm Yan'er."
Xi Rongyan was in that instant truly softened by the Emperor's tenderness. She felt with certainty that the Emperor genuinely cared for her.
Her hand hesitated, then moved — and wound lightly around the Emperor's waist. It was her bashful reply.
That careful, tentative initiative made something stir in Wei Qi's eyes.
This was the first time Xi Rongyan had ever held him of her own will. A tide rose in his heart — this feeling was greater than any compulsion he had ever used.
So this was what he had wanted. What he had sought.
Wei Qi's fingers actually trembled with a little excitement. His burning eyes were fixed on the person in his arms: "May I kiss you?"

chapters.title: I Have Long Been Fond of You
chapters.content:
The Emperor's burning breath fell right before her. His fingers were still caressing her cheek.
Those eyes were so gentle — as though she were being held with the most careful tenderness, and he would even ask before pressing his lips to hers.
He was the Emperor, the Son of Heaven.
Xi Rongyan's mind was in turmoil. In her daze, she found herself nodding before she knew it.
She felt her cheeks were very hot — perhaps because the Emperor's gaze was so intense that she found it hard to bear. She shyly, bashfully averted her eyes.
But in the next moment, her chin was lifted, her lips were kissed by the Emperor, and a heavy shadow fell over her. She was pressed beneath him.
She opened her eyes carefully. She saw those long eyes also watching her. She quickly closed her eyes again.
The Emperor's kiss was very light, grazing her lips, as though drawing her in little by little. He kissed the corner of her mouth, then along her jaw, then moved downward.
Xi Rongyan trembled. She felt her collar being drawn open, the exposed skin suddenly cool against the air, and then quickly covered by the warmth of his breath.
The damp kisses made a strange, unfamiliar heat rise in her body. Her eyes shimmered with tears, and she could not help an instinctive urge to resist and pull away.
Wei Qi's dark eyes watched the pale and lovely sight before him, his gaze always keeping a careful watch on Xi Rongyan's reactions. When he kissed down to her collarbone, he went no further.
Even though if he only tugged a little more at her collar, the view he longed for would be entirely revealed.
He had desired this body in countless nights. But now Wei Qi understood — what he wanted was for Xi Rongyan to willingly love him.
He was careful and patient. He stopped at the right moment. From the slight, involuntary flinch of her body just now, he knew she was not yet ready in her heart.
He pulled her waist close, returned to kissing her lips, and lingered there in tenderness with her. She did not resist — that was enough.
Yet no matter how much Wei Qi restrained himself, he still could not resist the body's instinctive response.
Afraid of frightening her, he lifted himself slightly away — only then daring to let himself give in to his body's response.
The feeling was both aching and exquisite, tormenting him, and yet in that torment he savored the joy of kissing his beloved.
Now the night had grown deep. Xi Rongyan felt, in truth, that she had been kissed until her lips were a little sore.
And she was a little breathless.
She pushed at the Emperor's chest and began to squirm.
She then heard the Emperor give a muffled groan. When she opened her eyes, she saw the Emperor's forehead was beaded with sweat, his eyes shut, as though he were in considerable pain.
She hurriedly asked in alarm: "Your Majesty, what is wrong?"
Wei Qi opened his eyes. Seeing Xi Rongyan's blank, anxious expression, he endured the ache and simply said: "Nothing."
With that, he rose and called for the maids outside to bring water. He then wrapped his robe around himself and went out.
Xi Rongyan watched the Emperor's retreating figure for a long while without understanding what had happened.
But she was already very drowsy. She yawned, pulled the quilt tightly around herself, and without even thinking about waiting for the Emperor to return, she closed her eyes and was asleep.
When Wei Qi came back after bathing, he found a figure bundled into a ball. He smiled helplessly.
He went over and lifted the quilt aside. Perhaps a draft had entered — the person inside instinctively moved toward him, leaning close.
The sleeping face was still well-behaved. Her head rested tightly against his chest, and her hands were like eyes that could see — finding and gripping his sleeve.
Wei Qi softened involuntarily. His gaze traced the lines of her face. His finger skimmed her cheek — plump, smooth, and yielding.
He thought of the Xi Rongyan of the previous life after they had married: even as a mother, her eyes had still been clear and innocent, still untouched by the ways of the world.
She had not truly changed much. The image of her face in his heart had never really changed.
Wei Qi leaned down lightly and breathed in the scent of her. His fingers moved involuntarily down toward her waist — and then he deliberately stilled them. He only pulled her tightly against him.
When Xi Rongyan woke in the morning, she was startled by what was pressed against her from behind.
The image from the book Yuzhu had shown her and the words her mother had told her flashed to mind. Her face flushed crimson in an instant.
She carefully tried to inch forward. The arm at her waist tightened and pulled her back. She stiffened — too afraid to move.
She suddenly felt a small sense of relief. At least the Emperor had only held her.
Behind her, Wei Qi smiled with his eyes.
He did not tease her further. He turned her over to face him, and looked at the cheeks so flushed they seemed about to drip red. He raised a brow and stroked her face with deliberate innocence: "What is the matter? Your face is so red."
Xi Rongyan wanted to find a hole to sink into. She cast about for an excuse: "It's a little warm..."
Wei Qi smiled. Looking at that small face half-buried in the dark hair — he found this Xi Rongyan altogether charming, so green she knew nothing.
Like a bud still unopened — all the more enticing for it.
His gaze fell on those half-parted red lips. His eyes grew still deeper. But he only pressed his lips lightly to her forehead and murmured: "Sleep a little longer."
"If you don't want to go to the Empress's palace, you don't have to."
Xi Rongyan stared wide-eyed at Wei Qi. The Empress's palace — could she truly not go?
Those apricot eyes went wide and bright, soft and dewy as flower petals in the morning. Wei Qi smiled: "You didn't sleep well last night. It doesn't matter if you skip it."
"I will have someone inform the Empress."
Xi Rongyan was speechless for a moment, then suddenly she wanted to ask why the Emperor treated her so well.
But the question that came out was: "That day at the Flower Viewing Festival — did this concubine do something to offend Your Majesty?"
Wei Qi's dark eyes shifted. Seeing Xi Rongyan bring this up now, he gave a quiet laugh. His fingers settled at her waist and asked: "Yan'er doesn't remember?"
Xi Rongyan bit her lip and shook her head.
She truly could not remember at all.
Wei Qi smiled: "That day, Yan'er threw her arms around me and even kissed me first."
He then sighed: "I tried to stop her, but Yan'er leaned in and said she had long admired me, and wanted to offer herself..."
He never got to finish the sentence, because his lips were covered by a pair of soft, white, fragrant palms.
His dark eyes held a smile as they looked at the person whose face had gone red all the way to the roots of her ears. He watched as those soft hands slowly released him, and the face went burrowing into the quilt, and a muffled, mosquito-thin voice came out: "Can Your Majesty please forget..."
Wei Qi laughed. It had never occurred to him that this Xi Rongyan would be so shy and sweet.
He had always thought her characteristically reserved and proper — and a little stubborn.
He lifted one edge of the quilt and looked at the exposed corner of her face — pale as magnolia, the tip of one ear faintly pink.
His long finger touched it lightly. He spoke softly: "Yan'er need not be embarrassed. I feel the same toward you."
"I have long been fond of you."
Xi Rongyan, buried in the quilt, went still. She turned her head and saw the Emperor's smiling eyes.
In those deep eyes was a warmth not unlike what Yunyu-gege once had when he looked at her. She was a little confused, and felt her heart suddenly beating fast.
The Emperor said he also felt fondness for her.
Had felt it for a long time.
But she and the Emperor...
Her mind went blank. She did not know how to react.
The shadow above her drew close as she was still dazed, and she was pulled tightly into that warm embrace once more. The Emperor's husky voice came from above: "I only hope that Yan'er truly meant what she said that day — that she is fond of me."
"I will not fail you. I will slowly give you every honor there is."
"Yan'er need only trust me."

chapters.title: You Are the Only One I Love
chapters.content:
The amber light, and everything within it, was so warm.
Above her was the Emperor's burning breath. Before her was the Emperor's broad chest.
Her heart slowed a beat, and in her memory the Emperor she had known began slowly to seem a stranger.
The Emperor before her was so gentle he felt like an error in her memory.
A helpless shyness spread unstoppably across her face. She was adrift in the Emperor's tender words, unable to form a thought, even forgetting to react.
Her eyes shifted like begonias in the wind, trembling and delicate, moving the heart.
Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan's lost, flushed face and was deeply satisfied.
He asked nothing more. He only wanted her not to fear him.
If not for the ongoing conflict in the north that needed to be brought under control first, he might well have moved directly to secure the position of Empress for her — to win her absolute trust.
But it did not matter. One day she would see his sincerity.
She had hated him wholly in the previous life. Every kindness he had shown her, she had refused to see. This time, starting over, he would give her enough time to finally understand his heart.
Just then Gao Yi's prompting voice drifted in from outside again. Wei Qi felt a flash of irritation.
He had never loathed rising early so much as he did now.
He held her a moment longer before getting up and going out to dress. He did not ask Xi Rongyan to help him this time.
Xi Rongyan watched the Emperor's retreating figure. The words he had just spoken were still circling in her head, leaving her in a daze.
She came back to herself quickly, rose, and went out. Even if the Emperor had not asked her to come help him dress, as one of the Emperor's consorts, she could not forget what was expected of her.
Xi Rongyan was not one to be spoiled by favor, and was even less willing to make mistakes. So she followed him out.
Outside, Xi Rongyan saw the palace servants helping Wei Qi into his outer robe. The black and gold dragon-embroidered imperial court robes settled over him, his back to the candlelight, his face half in shadow — noble and magnificent.
Even after the Emperor had just spoken so gently to her, without a smile his bearing was severe and cool, and impossible to approach.
Xi Rongyan steadied her thoughts and was about to walk forward when those deep eyes looked her way.
The expression that had been somewhat cold just a moment ago instantly softened. He smiled — actually smiled — and gestured to her: "Yan'er."
Xi Rongyan said a soft "mm" and walked over. The moment she did, warmth pressed around her.
The Emperor had pulled her into his arms.
Wei Qi held the slight figure, bent down, and smoothed a stray strand of hair from her cheek, tucking it behind her ear. He said with tender concern: "The spring chill hasn't passed. Next time, don't bother getting up."
Xi Rongyan's fingers rested on the Emperor's chest, lightly tracing the dragon embroidery. She said in a low, yielding voice — the manner of a consort doing her duty: "This concubine wishes to help Your Majesty dress."
Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan in silence for a long moment. He had never imagined there would come a day when Xi Rongyan would offer to dress him on her own initiative.
Even if he knew Xi Rongyan was perhaps only doing it because of her station, fulfilling the role of consort — a warmth rose in him all the same.
Whatever the reason, as long as Xi Rongyan was willing to come close to him, it was already more than enough.
But Wei Qi knew Xi Rongyan was sensitive to cold. Even in summer, her hands were always cool.
To have her up at this hour, in the dark of early morning, to dress him — it was not something he had the heart to ask of her. He did not want her to rise so early and attend him like this.
He sighed, and simply swept her into his arms and carried her back to the bed.
He set her down and looked at that captivating face, black hair spread across the pillow, the soft candlelight touching her eyes, which shone with a faint glow.
