His hands lingered in her dark hair with reluctant fondness, and he breathed in the scent of her deeply before pulling away. Then he said in a husky voice: "From now on, you need not rise with me. I have told you — you and I are like an ordinary husband and wife."
"In your presence, I am not the Emperor. You need not fear me or try to please me."
Wei Qi bent and pressed his lips lightly to Xi Rongyan's. In her dazed eyes, he caressed the corner of her eye: "Yan'er — you are the only person I love most in the world. Every word I have spoken to you has been something I truly wanted to say."
Wei Qi let his eyes rest on Xi Rongyan for one long moment, and then, to the sound of Gao Yi's calling voice once more from outside, he straightened and left.
After the Emperor left, Xi Rongyan unconsciously sat up. The quilt slipped to her waist. Her ankle-length hair fell over her chest. She sat in her reverie and raised a hand to her face, where the warmth of the Emperor's gentle touch still seemed to linger, faintly burning.
Yuzhu came in from outside, looked at Xi Rongyan's lost expression, and smiled with delight: "Mistress, the Emperor truly loves you."
Then she asked carefully: "Last night, it was the middle of the night when the Emperor called for water — did the Emperor take you as his own?"
Only then did Xi Rongyan come back to herself. She looked at Yuzhu and said quietly: "The Emperor has still not touched me."
Yuzhu was stunned. She stared at Xi Rongyan in disbelief: "The Emperor hasn't touched you for two nights?"
Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze, her fingertips tracing the embossed pattern in the silk quilt, her expression serene. She said quietly: "Don't worry. I know what I'm doing."
Because Xi Rongyan could see that the Emperor had refrained out of consideration for her feelings — not out of lack of desire.
So she was not troubled by it.
Yet Yuzhu was very worried: "How can the Emperor go on not touching mistress?"
In her heart she very much wanted to ask whether the Emperor had some ailment.
A woman like their mistress — her reputation for beauty had spread even in her girlhood home. It was impossible the Emperor did not want to touch her.
Xi Rongyan glanced at Yuzhu. As though reading what she was imagining, she said quietly: "Stop asking. Go draw water so I can wash up."
"Then call Baozhu in to help me dress."
Only then did Yuzhu quickly nod, and turned to go call for someone to bring water.
Wei Qi returned to Xuanzheng Hall. The hall was already lit up with candles, bright and warm throughout.
Several trusted ministers for the morning briefing were already waiting outside. Wei Qi clasped his hands behind him, looked out the window, and gave a quiet order: "Every word Consort Zhen says during today's morning attendance at the Empress's palace is to be reported back to me without omission."
Wei Qi knew Xi Rongyan well. Though he had told her she need not go to the Empress's palace, he knew her nature — she kept strictly to propriety and would almost certainly go regardless.
Thinking of the redness he had seen in her eyes yesterday, he wondered what grievances she had suffered among those women.
Gao Yi had long since ceased to be surprised by the Emperor's attentiveness toward Consort Zhen.
If the Emperor told him right now that he was deposing the Empress to install Consort Zhen in her place, he thought he would find it unremarkable.
Where once the Emperor had never had to be prompted, he had already been reminded several times in Consort Zhen's palace.
A scene like this had never played out in any other consort's quarters.
He replied with a quick "yes" and went at once to make arrangements.
Wei Qi then summoned the head palace attendant from Hanyuan Hall, Attendant Ling, to come and speak with him.
Attendant Ling came quickly, head bowed, waiting anxiously for the Emperor's questions.
Wei Qi glanced at the person kneeling on the floor, then calmly asked about every aspect of Xi Rongyan's daily life.

chapters.title: A Special Imperial Grace
chapters.content:
Attendant Ling reported everything Xi Rongyan had done in Hanyuan Hall from the day before until this morning — in full detail, nothing left out.
Wei Qi turned the thumb ring on his finger, thinking that once the conflict in the north was resolved, it would be time to clear out those women in the inner palace.
Meanwhile, Xi Rongyan had indeed gone and tidied herself to attend the Empress.
She had always been one to observe propriety, and it was not possible for her to simply not go — that would only draw the stares of all those women in the inner palace once more.
But when she stepped outside, she found an imperial palanquin waiting for her. Xi Rongyan did not get in.
By protocol, only consorts of the rank of Imperial Consort and above were permitted to ride a palanquin within the palace grounds. Others required a special imperial grace to do so.
Halfway along her route, she came to an intersection and saw, at some distance, Imperial Consort Qi riding in a palanquin toward her. Xie Yumian followed close behind, walking step by step.
Seeing this sight, Xi Rongyan did not know what to feel. She now understood one of the reasons why her cousin had wanted to move to her palace.
She found herself wondering — if the Emperor had not arranged for her to have Guanju Palace to herself, would she be walking in the same way? She thought she probably would not have been as cautious or deferential as that.
Imperial Consort Qi, riding the palanquin ahead, had already spotted Xi Rongyan. She saw her standing there in a pale ivory orchid cloak, no gold pins in her hair — only a jade ornament or two — and at her ears the same pair of jade drops as always.
Standing quietly, her face gentle and serene, fine brows and red lips, slender and graceful. In Imperial Consort Qi's eyes, the sight was grating.
She muttered a low curse about a fox spirit.
No one knew what tricks she used on the bed to keep the Emperor tied to her. On the outside she kept up this pretense of untouched purity.
She held her head high, disdaining to look at Xi Rongyan, and when Xi Rongyan bowed respectfully to her, she gave her a perfunctory glance and went on.
Xi Rongyan had not heard what Imperial Consort Qi had muttered. She waited for Xie Yumian at the back.
When Xie Yumian saw Xi Rongyan waiting for her, she felt a flicker of hesitation.
Yesterday she had visited Xi Rongyan's quarters and on her return had been summoned to Imperial Consort Qi's chambers, where she endured a round of cold mockery and had her allowance docked besides.
Almost everyone in the inner palace was on the Empress's side. Even the servants in the Internal Affairs Bureau knew how to read the room — with one word from Imperial Consort Qi, those attendants found ways to make her life difficult. The things sent to her were either spoiled or of the worst quality, and her food arrived cold.
All inner palace affairs fell under the Empress's authority. The Emperor had never visited her quarters. Whatever hardship she endured, she could only suffer in silence.
If Imperial Consort Qi saw her speaking with Xi Rongyan again right now, she would be made to suffer for it when she returned.
But she knew what Xi Rongyan was like — she had never harbored ill intentions toward anyone. It was she herself who had been worn down in two years of the palace's grinding, and was no longer who she had been.
Had she known that the Emperor she had glimpsed at a glance — a man like heaven itself — would be so cold-hearted, so void of desire, she would never have let herself hope.
Back in the capital, she had had some standing among the daughters of noble families. She had been proud and high-spirited, believing herself sure to be that one special woman — that when she entered the palace, the Emperor would love and favor her above all others, and bring glory to her entire family.
Now, all that hope was dead.
She could only bitterly regret her own ignorance.
Xi Rongyan, reading the hesitation on Xie Yumian's face, and then seeing her steal a careful glance at Imperial Consort Qi ahead — who turned and looked back at Xie Yumian with an expression of cold displeasure — understood her cousin's concern.
She did not linger. She began to walk on ahead. But behind her, Xie Yumian called out: "Sister."
Xi Rongyan turned. She saw Xie Yumian coming toward her, and asked quietly: "Walking with me — will it cause trouble for you? I would not want to put you in a difficult position."
Xie Yumian paused. So she had seen through it all.
She looked into Xi Rongyan's clear eyes.
Those black-and-white apricot eyes, whenever they looked at someone, always made that person feel as though they were her most cherished confidant.
In their girlhood she had always loved those eyes. Now they stirred a different feeling in her.
She recalled seeing the Emperor come to share noon meal with her yesterday, and a desolate feeling arose in her, unbidden.
She smiled, and walked beside Xi Rongyan: "It's nothing. Everyone knows you and I are close."
Xi Rongyan gave a quiet nod, but felt as though she had swallowed a fish bone.
Xie Yumian then asked: "Sister, last night's attendance — was it smooth?"
As she spoke, her gaze passed briefly over the mark half-hidden at Xi Rongyan's collar, and she smiled: "The Emperor must be very fond of you."
Xi Rongyan, hearing her cousin suddenly ask this, shook her head. "Sister, don't tease me."
Xie Yumian gave a faint smile to herself.
Xi Rongyan then said quietly: "Yesterday I spoke to the Emperor about having you move to my palace. But the Emperor said he would think it over, so I don't know if he will agree."
Xie Yumian looked at Xi Rongyan's earnest expression and lowered her head gently: "It doesn't matter."
She then asked: "Will the Emperor come to your quarters again tonight?"
Xi Rongyan shook her head: "I don't know either."
Xie Yumian glanced at the half-hidden mark at Xi Rongyan's collar and pressed her lips together.
She had been in the palace two years. The Emperor had visited her quarters only once.
And the Emperor had not touched her then either. He had only come and sat for a short while before leaving.
She had tried everything, and yet nothing had worked. To this day she still did not understand what she had done wrong that one night to displease the Emperor.
Xie Yumian forced a smile. She had no more words.
At the gate of the Empress's palace, Xie Yumian gave Xi Rongyan a gentle nudge. She said softly: "Your place is further forward, sister. Go ahead of me."
Xi Rongyan glanced at Xie Yumian's expression, then nodded and went ahead.
They were not the last to arrive, but Xi Rongyan felt the moment she stepped in, all eyes were fixed upon her.
What was strange was that today the women who had been coldly mocking her yesterday were strangely quiet.
She went forward to greet the Empress with proper decorum. The Empress smiled warmly and had her take a seat.
Xi Rongyan removed her outer cloak and passed it to Baozhu behind her, then sat down. Across from her, Imperial Consort Qi cast a glance at Xi Rongyan, then looked away.
She looked around at the others. Though their expressions were not warm, they were unusually quiet.
Xi Rongyan understood something in that moment.
These women all followed the Empress's lead.
Yesterday it was also only after the Empress's people spoke first that the others followed. Today, with the Empress's people staying silent, none of them dared to say anything.
When everyone was assembled, the Empress began the usual morning admonishments and reminders of palace rules.
The Empress held herself with natural poise, seated above them all, a presence before which one could not help but feel conviction.
Xi Rongyan glanced around and began to understand the general shape of things.
The four Imperial Consorts and the Empress had all been with the Emperor since he was still a prince. Imperial Consort Qi and Noble Consort Xian were both daughters of northern military commanders — naturally they were the Empress's faction.
No wonder everyone deferred so completely to the Empress.
No wonder the Empress Dowager had said: the inner palace was the Empress's domain.
In truth, Xi Rongyan had not found it strange. The Empress was, after all, the Empress — the woman who had been the Emperor's wife since his youth, who had given him the eldest and legitimate prince, whose family was powerful and prominent. No one could shake the Empress's position.
She understood why the Empress had been deliberately, if subtly, making things difficult for her. She only sighed at the narrowness of the Empress's mind.
The Empress above her looked over at Xi Rongyan from time to time, and then suddenly spoke: "Consort Zhen — you stay behind."

chapters.title: Imperial Favor
chapters.content:
The moment Xi Rongyan heard the Empress ask her to stay, she guessed it was about Noble Consort Xian again.
Sure enough, the Empress first smiled pleasantly and graciously seated her beside her, then brought up the matter of Noble Consort Xian.
Xi Rongyan responded with proper decorum: "This concubine has not yet had the opportunity to raise the matter of Noble Consort Xian."
A languid, drawn-out voice replied: "Oh?"
The Empress turned one of her long golden fingertip covers idly, watching Xi Rongyan with a faint smile: "It seems Consort Zhen must have had a tiring night serving the Emperor."
Xi Rongyan looked up and replied: "His Majesty came to bathe for the night and then slept. This concubine did not dare disturb him."
In truth, whether to intercede or not was not something Xi Rongyan cared much about. For one, the Emperor's decision had not been made at her instigation. Moreover, the punishment had been so severe that she suspected it was not solely because of that day's incident — there might be other reasons she was unaware of. She saw no need to try to change the Emperor's mind.
For another, even if she did intercede and the Noble Consort was pardoned, all would be well enough — but if she was not pardoned, the Empress would say she had not tried hard enough, and she would be criticized either way.
Better, then, to be straightforward about it.
Song Helan had not expected Xi Rongyan to speak so directly. She studied her for a moment. A cold light passed through her eyes, then quickly her voice warmed again: "I was only asking casually. I meant nothing by it."
"Your relationship with the Xie Cairen is like my relationship with Noble Consort Xian. I was simply concerned, that is all."
With that, Song Helan reached for a box from the maid beside her, opened it, and took out an exquisitely carved gold and jade bracelet. She clasped it onto Xi Rongyan's wrist and smiled: "You are the first to have the Emperor's favor for two nights running. This is your good fortune, and it gladdens me as well."
"This bracelet is a token of my sincerity. I also hope you will bear the Emperor a prince soon and bring us all a cause to celebrate."
Xi Rongyan looked at the bracelet on her wrist. Her mind had not yet fully processed what to make of it, and she quickly rose to thank the Empress.
Song Helan helped Xi Rongyan up, smiled warmly as she looked her over, and said: "Noble Consort Xian's behavior was indeed wrong, and I am sorry you were put through that. But do not dwell on it."
"Even if you choose not to petition on her behalf, I will not blame you."
"Let the matter be settled. I will not bring it up with you again — her fate is her own to bear."
Today the Empress's manner was somewhat different from yesterday's. Xi Rongyan gave a measured read of the situation and quickly offered her thanks.
After leaving the Empress's palace, Yuzhu immediately urged Xi Rongyan to take the bracelet off.
Xi Rongyan understood that Yuzhu suspected the bracelet might have been tampered with. But thinking over the Empress's outwardly gentle demeanor, she did not believe the Empress would resort to something so obvious.
Yuzhu thought it through and said: "Mistress, you have only just received the Emperor's favor. Do you truly think the Empress would wish you to bear the Emperor a prince?"
"This servant wonders — the Emperor is twenty-five. With a harem of women, however few, it seems the succession should not be so thin."
Even without Yuzhu pointing it out, Xi Rongyan had not intended to wear it. She took it off and had Yuzhu put it away carefully.
Over in Yongchun Palace, the Empress summoned Imperial Consort Qi, Noble Consort Li, and Consort Hui.
Imperial Consort Qi spoke first: "Your Highness is truly going to let her go on being favored like this?"
"How many times in a year does the Emperor come to the inner palace? At this rate, if she carries a dragon child, and the Emperor should one day..."
Imperial Consort Qi did not dare finish the thought, but she meant every word.
They had followed the Emperor since he was a prince, without ever being truly favored. But they understood — their interests and the Empress's were intertwined. If the Empress fell, they would all fall with her.
Consort Hui also chimed in: "This servant has never seen the Emperor favor any woman so openly. When the Emperor was still a prince and away in the north, one could understand it. But now the Emperor has been on the throne three years. How many women in this inner palace can barely catch a glimpse of him?"
"What exactly does this Consort Zhen have? It's just some fox spirit tricks."
"If the Emperor is truly bewitched, and the Empress Dowager stirs things along from behind — would she not think herself high above everyone else?"
"She wouldn't even look the Empress in the eye by then."
Song Helan tapped her fingers on the table, sitting upright, the phoenix pins in her hair glittering gold. Her normally gentle face now held a faint edge of coldness.
The Emperor had come to her yesterday — a rare occurrence — and in his casual words she had heard a warning.
Still about Xi Rongyan.
She glanced at Consort Hui and said coolly: "You needn't say such things to me. The Emperor arranged for her to be at Hanyuan Hall personally, with Chief Eunuch Gao overseeing all her needs. Why? To ensure she is not wronged."
"The Emperor may well see your every move. Remember what I told you yesterday — do not act rashly. Keep up a pleasant front toward Consort Zhen as well."
"Noble Consort Xian is the Emperor's warning to all of you and to me. Do not think the Emperor can be easily deceived. This Xi Rongyan is not like the women brought in through the selection years before."
"Those women the Emperor paid no mind to, rarely came to the inner palace, and you could do as you liked with them. But Xi Rongyan was brought in by imperial decree, fetched here by Gao Yi personally. Do you still not understand? Right under the Emperor's nose, we cannot touch her."
Noble Consort Li looked at the Empress: "What then? Are we to just watch her be favored?"
Song Helan gave her a sidelong look and smiled coldly: "If we don't make a move, what about others?"
"Take Wang Xiuyi, for instance — she once enjoyed the Emperor's attention."
Then Song Helan smiled again: "And there is Xi Rongyan's cousin, Xie Yumian."
Imperial Consort Qi was startled. She looked at the Empress: "Xie Cairen? I wouldn't think so."
"I've heard those two were very close before. They are cousins too — she shouldn't make a move against her own family."
Song Helan smiled: "The closer one was to a friend before, when watching that friend become more and more favored, what do you suppose one feels?"
"Wait and see. The Emperor will only favor that woman more as time goes on. By then, will Xie Cairen not feel like a clown in comparison?"
"Her own good friend is the apple of the Emperor's eye, while she herself cannot get even the scraps of his attention. What do you think she feels?"
"Someone like the Emperor would never give Xie Yumian a second glance just because he favors Consort Zhen."
Imperial Consort Qi was still a little doubtful: "But before, I treated Xie Cairen rather..."
Song Helan raised a brow: "That doesn't matter. Win her over gradually from now on."
"Drop a few words of insinuation in her ear, and over time even the deepest bond will crack."
Song Helan smiled again: "Besides, I can see clearly — Xie Yumian wants the Emperor's favor more than anyone."
"Back when Wang Xiuyi was in favor, she already showed signs of jealousy. How much more so now, with Consort Zhen — whom she has been close to like a sister?"
Consort Hui, who had been silent, nodded: "The Empress is right. When the Emperor was still in the prince's estate, he may not have managed the inner household affairs, but when something did happen, the Emperor saw through it all. No one dared to act out then. Even competing for favor was out of the question."
"Since we can't play games under the Emperor's eye, that's the wise approach."
"Wait until there is no other choice. Strike then."
"Better to watch those so-called refined and gentle noble women tear each other apart. Isn't that the better show?"
Noble Consort Li said nothing. She looked at the others, then nodded along.

chapters.title: Emotion Incense
chapters.content:
That afternoon, Xi Rongyan was summoned again by the Empress Dowager.
Upon learning that the Emperor had spent two consecutive days with her, the Empress Dowager was visibly pleased.
She passed Xi Rongyan a box with a smile: "It is your fortune that the Emperor favors you so. I have never seen the Emperor this attentive to anyone."
"Inside are vitality pills. Take one each day — they will help with conception."
Xi Rongyan opened the box and found small red medicine pills inside, faintly releasing a medicinal fragrance.
The Empress Dowager's wish for her to conceive a child quickly — she understood, and knew it was meant to protect her.
The Empress Dowager then looked at Xi Rongyan's plain attire and took her hand: "Why are you dressed so simply?"
Xi Rongyan looked up: "Your niece has only just entered the palace and does not wish to draw attention."
She then said quietly: "Now that the Emperor comes to my quarters often, keeping a low profile is to my advantage as well."
The Empress Dowager paused, then smiled: "Don't always think about keeping a low profile. Your opportunity is right here."
"You have only been in the palace two days, yet you have already surpassed someone who's been here two years."
"Take your cousin, for instance — the Emperor has never once favored her."
This was the first time Xi Rongyan had heard this.
Her cousin had never spoken to her of her situation with the Emperor in the palace. She was genuinely surprised.
She paused: "How can that be..."
The Empress Dowager smiled: "Did you think the Emperor must favor every woman in the inner palace?"
"Many of them will never lay eyes on the Emperor even once in their lives, growing old and dying within these palace walls."
"Those of lower rank do not even have the right to attend the Empress's morning gathering."
"In the past, women plotted desperately for the chance of a chance encounter with the Emperor — but none of them came to a good end."
The incense in the burner on the altar table coiled lazily in the still, quiet air. The Empress Dowager turned her teacup slowly and looked at Xi Rongyan's eyes with a measured, unhurried gaze: "Rongyan, the Emperor is spending his nights with you. That is your fortune."
"Your mother wrote to me about what happened at the Flower Viewing Festival. Do you think the Emperor would issue a decree to bring you into the palace if he had no intention of having you?"
"Knowing the Emperor's temperament, if you had offended him, he would have had you punished."
Xi Rongyan suddenly remembered what the Emperor had said to her this morning — that he had long been fond of her.
In truth, she found it difficult to believe.
The Emperor had left for the north at fifteen and earned considerable military merit. His returns to the capital had been rare. He had come back only when the late Emperor fell gravely ill at twenty-one, and it had been barely three years since then. The number of times the two of them had truly crossed paths was small.
Even when they had crossed paths, it had been nothing more than a passing exchange of pleasantries.
Before her thoughts had fully settled, the Empress Dowager dismissed the attendants around them. She then lifted another box from the side table and handed Xi Rongyan a bracelet, saying quietly: "This bracelet is hollow inside. It contains emotion incense."
"Wear it on your wrist when the Emperor comes. He will not be able to leave your side."
Xi Rongyan looked at the item and felt it was something she did not wish to hold.
The Empress Dowager frowned: "Rongyan, your aunt has been through everything in the inner palace these many years. Whatever methods exist, I have seen them all."
"The Emperor is a man, and men have desires. You are only amplifying that desire. Once you have a child, you will no longer need it."
"A man's love passes in an instant — if you do not seize this opportunity, it may not come again."
"Your aunt used this herself once. I conceived through this as well."
"Trust your aunt. How could I ever harm you?"
Xi Rongyan looked at the bracelet in the Empress Dowager's hand, her thoughts in turmoil.
She had come to the palace hoping for a quiet, settled life — but she did not want to use such means.
From what she had seen, the Emperor did not appear to be a man of excessive desire. Moreover, the Emperor was devoted to state affairs and spent little time in the inner palace to begin with. If the Emperor were to discover she had used something like this, it might well backfire.
But she hesitated for a long while, and in the end accepted it.
She would treat it as accepting her aunt's kind intention — to set her mind at ease.
When she returned, Xi Rongyan held the bracelet and examined it by the window. She lifted it to her nose and smelled it. There truly was a faint scent.
She could not quite describe it, but it was pleasant — and not easy to detect.
Baozhu, curious, asked: "Can it truly be so effective?"
Yuzhu looked at Xi Rongyan and asked: "The Empress Dowager's things should work well. If the Emperor comes tonight, perhaps you should try?"
But Xi Rongyan placed the bracelet in Yuzhu's hands and shook her head: "Put it away in the case. I do not wish to use it."
Yuzhu could only say: "Mistress, now that you are in the palace, you should at least think of your own future."
Xi Rongyan sat on the couch, turned her head, and said softly to Yuzhu: "I know you both wish me well. But I do not want to use such a method — and I fear it would do more harm than good."
"It has not come to that yet."
Yuzhu had no choice but to take it and put it away.
Xi Rongyan then called Baozhu over to look at her face. There was still a faint pink mark, but it was slowly fading — which was a relief.
That evening the Emperor came again. Xi Rongyan had just finished bathing. She tended to sleep early, had asked for the time, and thinking the Emperor would likely not come tonight, had already gotten into bed.
She had been propped up chatting with Baozhu when the palace maid outside hurried in with the announcement that the Emperor had arrived. She was briefly startled, and had just sat up when the Emperor's tall figure was already striding inside.
Baozhu, ever perceptive, quickly stepped back and withdrew.
The Emperor carried the chill of the night air with him as he entered, and the warm room seemed to grow cooler with his presence. That black-robed figure walking in made Xi Rongyan feel a breath of cold.
Wei Qi's gaze swept over Xi Rongyan's wrists, and he lowered his gaze without a word. He pulled her close, taking in the warmth of her body.
Xi Rongyan, held within the Emperor's arms, felt as though the Emperor knew she would feel cold and had pulled the quilt up around her waist.
The warmth of his palm covered her back.
By now she found the Emperor's scent familiar. She was no longer as afraid of him as she once had been. She had not expected the Emperor to come tonight. Listening to the quiet sigh at her ear, she looked up.
She saw the Emperor was also looking at her. In those cool, long eyes was the flicker of candlelight — and the reflection of her face.
Her heart wanted to take the initiative, yet she did not know how.
Even now, with the Emperor holding her so gently, she did not know how she ought to respond.
She hesitated, and then lightly leaned against the Emperor's chest. It was the only proactive gesture she could manage.
Wei Qi had not dared to hope Xi Rongyan would take any initiative. And yet she was actually leaning her soft body toward him.
His heart hammered. The fingers at her back actually trembled with excitement.
He suddenly cupped Xi Rongyan's face in his hands, looked at her quietly, his excitement flickering and dancing in the candlelight in his eyes.
The eardrops at her ear were brushing against his thumb ring, giving off a faint, clear, chiming sound — a sound like the coaxing notes of an intoxicating melody. Her face, luminous as the moon, was no longer a moon's reflection in the water — it was the real, warm sensation beneath his hands.
He could not hold himself back. Beneath that clear, innocent gaze, he bent his head and kissed her.
The fragrance on her body made his body taut. The soft warmth of her made the blood that had so long craved her surge. He pressed her against him, his hands moving across her body, no longer under his own control.

chapters.title: Did I Frighten You Just Now?
chapters.content:
Wei Qi's kisses were so heavy that Xi Rongyan could barely close her lips. Overcome, she let out a few soft sounds, yet she did not stop him.

The broad hand slipped beneath the hem of her robe — still carrying the coolness of his cuff — and Xi Rongyan shivered slightly at the chill.

She knew what might happen next.

Yuzhu had just had her carefully study the little manual, which was still under her pillow.

She also knew it would hurt. Her mother had said to endure — it would pass; every woman went through this, and it got better afterward.

Though Xi Rongyan was afraid, the Emperor's movements were urgent and heavy, and she felt a soreness even in her lips. But she told herself to endure — it would pass.

She dared not open her eyes. When the Emperor finally released her lips, she heard his suppressed, labored breathing at her ear.

Just like in the dream.

The man in that dream had breathed like this too.

The same heavy force.

She began to feel a faint trembling of fear again.

She barely opened her eyes — and found herself looking directly into the Emperor's gaze.

Those dark eyes were bottomless. Colored by desire, they turned a little fearsome, and in one particular moment they were exactly like the eyes in her dream.

In the dream, that man had bound her hands and made her whole body ache — an endless torment.

She could not tell dream from reality. The word came out of her without thinking: "No..."

Wei Qi's hands stilled in an instant.

He pulled himself from the flood of desire and saw Xi Rongyan's frightened eyes looking back at him.

Only a moment ago she had been so yielding beneath him, her fingers even resting lightly at his waist.

He had thought she was ready. Ready to give herself to him.

Why was she looking at him with such fear again?

Instinctively he glanced at his reflection in the nearby lamp column. He had been hiding his possessiveness of her perfectly well — yet the reflection there was warped and twisted, like a grotesque specter. Even he could not see clearly what he looked like in that moment.

The fingers that had been gripping Xi Rongyan's waist were white with tension. Wei Qi lowered his lashes, letting all the dark emotion sink into the shadows.

His half-removed outer robe hung loose on his shoulders. He bent down and gathered Xi Rongyan gently into his arms. Looking into her frightened eyes, without a trace of reproach, he pressed his lips softly to her forehead and asked in a low voice: "Did I frighten you just now?"

Xi Rongyan looked at the Emperor's eyes now — gentle, watching her. Her heart beat hard, and then a sudden wave of guilt rose in her.

She could not understand why she kept being haunted by that nightmare. The Emperor had been tender with her, yet she had blurted out those words just now, and the Emperor had not blamed her even so.

Xi Rongyan quickly shook her head, then lowered her eyes in shame, not daring to meet the Emperor's gaze. She said quietly: "Just now this concubine did not mean to..."

Wei Qi soothed her with patient care: "It's all right. I don't blame you."

"It was my own movements that were too rough."

Wei Qi lifted her chin and asked: "Did I hurt you just now?"

It had hurt, a little — the Emperor's movements had been heavy.

Xi Rongyan hesitated, and in the end did not admit it. She gave a small shake of her head. "No..."

Wei Qi had already read the answer in Xi Rongyan's earlier hesitation.

He also understood that Xi Rongyan still feared his station and dared not tell him the truth. This woman had always been timid, frightened of everything.

Yet she had been so devoted to that dead husband of hers — refusing to yield to him alone.

In the previous life, she had feared him, yet had still resisted him at every turn.

He pressed his lips together. His gaze fell to the red marks on Xi Rongyan's neck. His fingers gently drew aside one edge of her robe.

There were red marks on her waist too, from the force he had used.

Wei Qi paused, and bent down to press his lips tenderly to those marks, then looked up at her with remorse: "Yan'er, I'm sorry."

"I'll be gentler next time."

When the Emperor had pressed his lips to her waist just now, Xi Rongyan had trembled — that spot still carried a faint, lingering tingle.

She seemed to recall the Emperor saying something about being gentler before.

But Xi Rongyan had no experience with such things and did not know whether what the Emperor did was too rough or simply how things were.

She gave a small nod. The Emperor's fingers kneaded at her waist — such a light touch, yet she felt his tenderness clearly.

After a long while, Wei Qi let Xi Rongyan rest first while he went to bathe.

Xi Rongyan watched the Emperor's retreating figure and thought quietly that tonight would again come to nothing.

Though she felt a small pang of regret, she also felt a relieved exhale — as though she had escaped something. All together it was a tangle of complicated feelings.

She closed her eyes and again the dream scenes with that man came to her. She did not want to dream of him again, so she lay with her eyes open, willing herself to forget.

When Wei Qi came back, he was surprised to find Xi Rongyan still awake — as though she had been waiting for him.

His heart warmed. He pulled the warm, soft person into his arms and looked at her bashful, pale face. Without thinking, he softened his voice. "Were you waiting for me?"

In truth that had not been Xi Rongyan's intention — but seeing the Emperor's downward gaze, she instinctively nodded.

That obedient nod pleased Wei Qi. It was rare for her to know to wait for him — so she was not entirely indifferent to him after all.

His body was again threatening to run away from him. He suppressed the impulse and only lightly ran his fingers through her hair.

Seeing that the Emperor seemed to be in quite a good mood, Xi Rongyan weighed her words carefully before finally asking: "This concubine would like to have her cousin come and live in Guanju Palace. Would Your Majesty agree?"

This was already the second time Xi Rongyan had raised the matter.

Wei Qi gave a noncommittal murmur, his gaze passing over Xi Rongyan's face for a moment. Then, as if tired, he patted her back. "Sleep now."

Xi Rongyan paused. With an answer like that, she could not tell whether the Emperor had agreed or not.

She hesitated and looked up again. "Has Your Majesty agreed?"

Wei Qi looked down at her and thought for a moment about how to discourage her without making her unhappy.

He did not want Xi Rongyan to be disappointed, but he also did not want her cousin coming here.

Setting aside Xie Yumian's dubious motives from the previous life, he also had no wish for Xi Rongyan to be drawn back into memories of her time with Gu Yunyu.

Xie Yumian's presence would inevitably stir up some of those recollections.

He wanted Gu Yunyu to become the past, completely and thoroughly.

Wei Qi regretted it a little — he had forgotten about Xie Yumian. Had he remembered earlier, he would have sent her away long ago.

His fingertips shifted at her waist. After a brief silence, he said quietly: "This matter has been left for the Empress to arrange. I have already given her instructions."

Hearing the Empress mentioned, Xi Rongyan knew in her heart this would likely be difficult. Yet the Emperor had already said as much, and it would seem unreasonable to press further.

She knew Imperial Consort Qi was the Empress's ally, and was not sure the Empress would arrange anything at all. The uncertainty sat in her heart.

She was most afraid that Imperial Consort Qi would know, and make things difficult for her cousin.

She was about to speak again when the Emperor had already reached up to lower the bed curtain. The heavy drape shut out the light from outside, and the Emperor's husky voice came from above her head: "Are you settling in well here in the palace?"

Xi Rongyan faintly understood the Emperor did not wish to continue that conversation. She could only set aside the matter of her cousin for now and answered softly: "Yes, well enough."

The Emperor seemed to have asked only in passing. He gave a single murmur of assent and said nothing more.

It was Xi Rongyan who could not sleep — turning from side to side, unable to settle.

Wei Qi opened his eyes in the dark and glanced at the person in his arms who was still awake. He held her waist to keep her from fidgeting, then drew her over to lie against his chest and asked: "Can't sleep?"

Xi Rongyan lay half-propped against Wei Qi's chest and said quietly: "There is no one to talk to in this palace. It's cold and lonely."

As she said it, she nuzzled her face against Wei Qi's chest in something almost like a pout, her arms circling his broad, firm waist. She even rubbed her face gently against him — which made Wei Qi's breath catch.

chapters.title: A Rare Initiative
chapters.content:
Wei Qi knew perfectly well why Xi Rongyan was doing this.

It was rare for her to take such initiative.

But it was only for the sake of someone else that she could be this attentive and persistent.

He pressed his lips together and said nothing. Her soft body made him taut all over — especially because she was wearing only thin clothes, and she pressed against him with no idea at all how enticing that was.

Perhaps she truly believed he would not touch her.

He quietly looked down at her. In his heart, he had already begun to relent. In the end, he could not bear to let her down.

In the previous life he had desperately wished she would be able to coax him like this. But she had never once done so.

His fingers settled in her dark hair. He sighed quietly. "I will arrange it. Just wait a few more days."

Hearing the Emperor's words, the anxiousness that had been sitting in Xi Rongyan's heart eased a little. She held him tighter and said softly: "This concubine thanks Your Majesty."

Wei Qi silently tugged at the corner of his mouth. His fingers slid from her hair down to her waist. "Is there anything else you want to say to me?"

In fact, Xi Rongyan did.

She brought up what the Empress had said to her about Noble Consort Xian, then added quietly: "About the Noble Consort's matter, Your Majesty..."

Her voice trailed off into a low laugh from the Emperor.

She looked up but could not make out the Emperor's expression in the dark — she did not understand why he had laughed.

She only heard his low voice: "Even if I release her, she will not believe it was you who pleaded for her."

"This is something I wanted to do long before — punishing Noble Consort Xian is not your concern. I will speak with the Empress about it."

Xi Rongyan paused at that, and then felt reassured.

She nodded and leaned comfortably back against the Emperor's chest.

She found herself puzzled. The Emperor always spoke to her gently, as though he was never truly angry. She was genuinely no longer so afraid of him, and found that having him near actually gave her a feeling of calm in which she could fall asleep.

She had always been cold-blooded since childhood — even in spring she needed a warming jar inside her quilt. The Emperor was warm, and held in his arms through the night she would not feel cold once.

She felt the Emperor press his lips to her forehead — soft, warm, and tender. Her heart skipped a beat. The fingers resting against his chest tightened of their own accord, and she closed her eyes in peace.

When Wei Qi woke the following morning, Xi Rongyan was still sleeping.

He looked at her for a long time — eyes closed, buried in his arms — then lightly touched her cheek. The warm, soft sensation made everything feel real.

He could not help but think of the moment she had left him, her body covered in blood.

Wei Qi closed his eyes, cutting off the thought, and quietly rose.

When Xi Rongyan finally woke with a start, she found the Emperor had long since gone.

In the days that followed, the Emperor continued to spend his nights at Hanyuan Hall.

Whispers ran through the inner palace, and the looks cast Xi Rongyan's way shifted again and again.

On one particular morning, as Xi Rongyan was leaving the Empress's palace hoping to find her cousin and talk with her about the move, someone suddenly blocked her path.

She looked over — she recognized the person by now, after all these days.

It was Wang Xiuyi — the one her mother had mentioned as the most favored woman in the inner palace.

Wang Xiuyi was, naturally, quite beautiful: delicate and graceful, wearing a peach-red spring dress, holding a jade-handled fan, jade bracelets on both wrists, her adornments chosen with great care.

But her brows were drawn up high, at odds with the otherwise gentle impression of her face.

Xi Rongyan had already guessed at some of Wang Xiuyi's hostility toward her.

Yet even though Wang Xiuyi regarded her with such antipathy, Xi Rongyan felt no displeasure at all.

Wang Xiuyi had been favored before. Perhaps it was Xi Rongyan's turn now. And after her, who would be next?

If one hated every woman who received favor, would there be enough hatred to go around?

As youth faded, younger and more beautiful women would continue to enter. By then, would the Emperor even remember the faces that had come before?

Xi Rongyan had no wish to be the target of anyone's hatred, so she asked in a soft voice: "Sister, do you have something you wished to say to me?"

Wang Xiuyi looked Xi Rongyan up and down. In truth she had seen her before, at banquets, though only from a distance.

Back then, Xi Rongyan had been the model and center of attention among the noble daughters — not only for her striking looks, but for her ever-gentle and refined manner.

She had always been impeccably gracious in company.

Her own elder brother had secretly liked her once. But unfortunately Xi Rongyan had already been engaged.

Wang Xiuyi had once wished to become someone like her — and had felt a quiet envy.

She still remembered one banquet where Xi Rongyan had worn only a simple blue orchid-patterned dress, yet she had gleamed in the sunlight. With the begonias in bloom, she had sat before the flowers and drawn every eye in the room.

Now she had entered the palace, and Wang Xiuyi knew herself to be no match for her. Yet she was not willing to accept it.

She had once been the only place in the inner palace the Emperor would visit — even though he had never touched her even then. But ever since Xi Rongyan had entered the palace, on the days that should have been the Emperor's visits to her, he had shown no intention of coming at all. She could not help the resentment in her heart.

The sisters who used to fawn over her now looked at her with tepid pity. The cutting and sarcastic remarks — she heard them all too clearly.

Even Imperial Consort Qi and Consort Hui, who had once been relatively civil with her, now barely acknowledged her.

The little eunuchs who used to rush to please her no longer came.

Even her daily meals, in just these few short days, had fallen far below what they used to be.

Of course she was bitter. How could she not be?

If Xi Rongyan had never entered the palace, none of this would have changed.

Wang Bao'ran squeezed her fingers tight. She wanted to contain the jealousy on her face, yet she could not.

The inner palace was like this — everyone was a quick reader of the room, always watching for cues. The moment the Emperor stopped visiting her, they changed their tune in an instant.

She took a deep breath and forced a smile. "I do have something I'd like to say to you."

"Would it be convenient for me to come sit with you for a while, sister?"

Seeing her expression, Xi Rongyan nodded and agreed.

Not far behind them, Imperial Consort Qi and Consort Hui watched Wang Xiuyi and Xi Rongyan walk away together. Consort Hui laughed. "Look at that — I had someone tamper with Wang Xiuyi's food just a few days ago, had people mock her for a couple of days, and she's already lost her composure."

Imperial Consort Qi gave a slow, lazy smile. "The Empress has the right idea. Let's just sit back and watch the show."

The two of them chatted and laughed as they turned and went their separate ways.

Not far away on the palace path, Xie Yumian stood watching Xi Rongyan and Wang Xiuyi walk away side by side. Her face went rigid.

She had assumed Xi Rongyan would actually make good on her word and bring her to Hanyuan Hall. With the Emperor staying there night after night, showing her such favor — she could not believe a request as simple as this would be refused.

Unless Xi Rongyan had never truly intended to help her at all. Perhaps she feared she would go to Guanju Palace and draw away the Emperor's attention.

Xie Yumian clutched the handkerchief in her hands until her knuckles went white. She kept her eyes on Xi Rongyan's retreating figure until it disappeared — and then the hatred that surfaced in her eyes was unmistakable.

Wang Bao'ran followed Xi Rongyan into Hanyuan Hall. Her gaze swept over every corner of the spacious palace, and seeing Xi Rongyan living here alone in such grandeur, the envy rose in her again, unstoppable.

The two of them sat down together. Wang Bao'ran looked at Xi Rongyan — and promptly reddened around the eyes. She pressed her handkerchief to them and bowed her head, letting the tears fall.

chapters.title: More and More Favored
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan was taken aback at Wang Bao'ran's behavior. She did not understand why she had burst into tears the moment she sat down, and quickly asked in a hushed voice: "Sister, what is the matter?"

Wang Bao'ran looked at Xi Rongyan through her tears, her voice choked. "Nothing. I only envy your good fortune, sister."

Xi Rongyan did not know what to say. She offered softly: "Sister need not envy me. You and I are not so different."

Wang Bao'ran wiped her tears. "Ever since the Emperor began going to you, I fear he has forgotten all about me — the one who was here first."

Xi Rongyan replied sincerely: "How does sister know I will not one day be the one who is forgotten?"

"Perhaps it will not be long before the Emperor stops coming to me as well."

Wang Bao'ran was startled, and stared at Xi Rongyan.

She saw Xi Rongyan sitting gracefully beside her, her face genuinely free of any satisfaction or gloating at being favored. By contrast, she felt like an undignified fool reaching for something out of her grasp.

Wang Bao'ran murmured in a daze: "Sister is joking. Who in the inner palace can compare to you right now?"

"Everyone can see the Emperor treats you differently."

Xi Rongyan did not wish to argue the point. She only said quietly: "Sister, whether you believe me or not, what I said came from my heart."

Wang Bao'ran stared at Xi Rongyan's face for a long moment.

She could find not one crack in her manner — as though the Emperor's favor truly meant very little to her.

She genuinely seemed unwilling to compete for it.

She was receiving so many benefits from that favor, yet here she was acting so serene and detached. What was the purpose of such a performance?

She suppressed the irritation in her heart, dried her tears, and gripped Xi Rongyan's hand tightly. "May I ask sister, what method you've used to keep the Emperor with you for so many consecutive days?"

Wang Bao'ran wept again. "I ask for nothing else — only for the Emperor to spend one night with me."

Xi Rongyan's hand was gripped so tightly it had begun to ache.

Looking at Wang Bao'ran's relentlessly tearful, heartbroken face, she felt another kind of sorrow entirely.

She had long known that she herself would also be locked inside these walls for the rest of her life. She had made her peace with being swallowed up among so many women.

If she could not be open-minded enough to let herself go, she would only live in misery.

Wang Xiuyi had clearly not been able to let herself go.

She thought: would she herself become this one day? Clinging to an obsession, unable to release it from her heart, only tormenting herself?

The thought filled her with dread for the future.

Something lodged in Xi Rongyan's throat. She bowed her head for a moment — the cold jade eardrops brushing her cheek, the string of white jade beads at her neck hanging in the air — and gently dabbed at Wang Bao'ran's tears with her handkerchief, knowing she could not help anyone.

As for Wang Bao'ran's true reason for coming to her, she had a vague sense of it — and did not think it was only for this.

Besides, to ask her what method she used to please the Emperor — was Wang Bao'ran truly so naïve, or did she simply think Xi Rongyan had no guard against her?

She said simply: "Sister, please do not grieve so. In truth, I have used no method whatsoever. Why the Emperor comes to my quarters, I myself do not understand."

"Sister has been in favor before — what could I possibly teach you?"

"But as we both live here in the inner palace, we could spend our days together in conversation and keep each other company."

A handkerchief scented with fragrance settled softly against Wang Bao'ran's eyes. She paused for a moment. Her gaze fell to the silver-threaded orchid fan on Xi Rongyan's lap.

She looked upward slowly — the neatly gathered collar, the gentle luster of the beads reflecting her own tears, and then above that, the composure beneath Xi Rongyan's beautifully drawn brows.

Poised, graceful, slender, lovely. Who would not be drawn to her?

That the Emperor liked her suddenly seemed not so hard to understand.

She suddenly felt that she could never, in all her life, be a match for her.

She did not have Xi Rongyan's fortune. From the moment of entering the palace, she had lived alone in her own hall with no faction pressing down on her, the Empress Dowager standing behind her. Even if she fell out of favor, the Empress would not dare go too far.

She was different.

A woman in the inner palace without the Emperor's love was no better than a nameless weed at the base of the palace wall — even a eunuch could tread on her. A whole year might pass without catching the Emperor's eye even once. If she died, she would be wrapped in white cloth and carried out.

It forced her to compete.

She did not have Xi Rongyan's family background or her standing.

A tear rolled down Wang Bao'ran's cheek. She spoke from her heart: "I am not like you, sister. I cannot afford to pass the days in such idle leisure."

"All I want is even a little of the Emperor's favor — just enough to live a little better in this palace."

Xi Rongyan looked at that single tear, her dark brows faintly raised then let go. She said quietly: "Sister entered the palace before me and should better understand the ways of survival here, and the Emperor's temperament. You would know I truly cannot help you."

Xi Rongyan could not even manage to bring her own cousin to live in Guanju Palace — how was she to help Wang Bao'ran?

In that moment, Wang Bao'ran suddenly understood.

Xi Rongyan was still the same gentle, well-bred lady she had always been. Everyone loved her — because she truly could nourish people like a soft spring rain.

Even though she had genuinely resented and envied her just now, there came a moment when, suddenly, she did not hate her anymore.

She knew what Xi Rongyan said was true. She understood even more that the Emperor was not someone who could be controlled by anyone.

And some people were simply born to have everything.

Even when the Gu family had its catastrophe and everyone mocked Xi Rongyan, she had turned around and entered the palace — and effortlessly won the Emperor's favor.

She could not hold back the tears. She bent her head and pressed it against Xi Rongyan's shoulder, sobbing. "May I come often and talk with you?"

Xi Rongyan had not expected Wang Bao'ran to lean on her like this. She felt a dampness at her shoulder, and said quietly: "Of course you may. I am lonely here alone."

When Wang Bao'ran finally left, she turned to look back at the peach blossoms filling the courtyard.

She had heard long ago that Xi Rongyan loved peach blossoms. That one backward glance, and she gave up completely.

Because she understood now that perhaps the Emperor truly loved Xi Rongyan — had planted this entire courtyard full of peach blossoms for her. She, who mattered so much to the Emperor, was perhaps the only one.

She had no more desire to compete. She even found herself hoping Xi Rongyan would grow more and more favored.

Between that Empress who looked gentle and kind on the surface yet was cold-hearted beneath — and Xi Rongyan — she found herself wanting Xi Rongyan to have the upper hand.

Then perhaps the inner palace would truly be peaceful.

Wang Bao'ran returned to Xingqing Palace.

The main hall there was occupied by Consort Hui; the Xiyu Hall on the other side housed Noble Lady Lin. Only she lived in the Jingyi Study — a narrow two-room western-facing apartment with poor light.

She could hear the sounds of Consort Hui and Noble Lady Lin laughing together in the main hall. She sat alone and cold at the window.

The palace maid standing behind her stepped forward and asked: "Did you not prepare something earlier, my lady? Why did you not give it to Consort Zhen?"

"If you had gotten rid of her, the Emperor would have come back to remember you again."

Wang Bao'ran looked at the palace maid. There was no real deference in those eyes — only a kind of reproach.

She was silent.

All the palace maids assigned to her after she entered the palace had been carefully chosen by the Empress. What could she say?

Her every step was watched by another's eyes.

A single misstep was all the Empress needed to deal with her — nothing could be easier.

Wang Bao'ran was quiet for a long while before saying softly: "Wait a little longer."

After Wang Bao'ran left, Xi Rongyan's mood was also subdued.

She sat sideways on the couch, gazing at the peach blossoms outside the window, lost in thought. Her fingers turned the fan, and Wang Bao'ran's tearful face drifted back before her eyes.

A sorrow stirred for her — the kind that lived in the deep places of the heart.

She propped her cheek on her hand beside the small table, sitting in this cold and exquisite palace hall, and looked at the old keepsake on her wrist that her mother had given her. As though that alone was her one remaining comfort.

Something that could remind her of the easier days that had come before.

In Xuanzheng Hall, Wei Qi listened to Gao Yi relay the news that Wang Bao'ran had gone to Hanyuan Hall to speak with Xi Rongyan. The fingers resting on the imperial desk paused.

chapters.title: Yan'er, Come Here
chapters.content:
Wei Qi had been visiting Wang Bao'ran once or twice a month in the past, and not for any other reason. He had taken up arms young and spent many years fighting campaigns — his knee had sustained some minor injuries, which now ached faintly from time to time.

Wang Bao'ran had a skilled hand with massage that could ease the pain a little.

It was not as though he specifically had to go to her; it was simply that Wang Bao'ran was relatively unobtrusive. She would not overstep or cling or attempt to charm him. She stayed quiet and still — far preferable to the women who chattered and vied for his attention.

Now Wei Qi found himself worrying that Wang Bao'ran might have said something to Xi Rongyan.

He was afraid Xi Rongyan might start thinking too much.

After all, in others' eyes, he had favored Wang Bao'ran.

His fingertips tapped the desk a few times, and then he gave Gao Yi a quiet instruction.

Gao Yi acknowledged it, lowered his head, and withdrew.

It was mid-afternoon now, the sky heavy and overcast.

Xi Rongyan was summoned to Xuanzheng Hall, not knowing what this was about.

When she entered, she saw only the Emperor seated at the high desk. Behind him stood the pillars carved with golden dragons — imposing and magnificent. The white jade floor tiles cast faint reflections. Incense coiled from the burners.

It was her first time here. Looking at the Emperor behind those towering stacks of memorials, his gold crown gleaming, his face commanding and dignified — so much more severe than the gentleness she saw from him daily — she hastily moved to kneel.

But the Emperor had already set down his papers and beckoned to her with a wave of his hand. "Yan'er. Come here."

Xi Rongyan hesitated, then walked to the Emperor's side.

Wei Qi took Xi Rongyan's hand and settled her on his knee. He looked carefully at the emotions in her face. Seeing her sitting with her head slightly lowered, not looking at him, her jade eardrops swaying gently, something tightened in his chest.

He noticed, too, the shadows beneath her long lashes — she seemed to be carrying something on her mind. He pressed her closer without a word.

He did not want her to fall into brooding, imagining that he cared for someone else.

But he did not want to ask her directly about Wang Bao'ran either — afraid she would overthink it and worry that he was watching her every move.

Wei Qi glanced at Gao Yi nearby. Gao Yi stepped outside and gestured. Moments later, several eunuchs came in with heads bowed, carrying a few trays.

Wei Qi waved one of them forward and pointed to a set of gold, silver, and kingfisher-feather flower-blossom headdress ornaments on the tray. He watched Xi Rongyan's expression and said quietly: "Look. Do you like them?"

Gao Yi stood to one side looking on. These were things the consorts in the palace had dreamed of for years — the Emperor had never bestowed them on anyone before. This time he had brought out the most beautiful pieces all at once, just to please Consort Zhen.

Xi Rongyan only needed one glance. She could see the hundred-flower crown was set all around with sea pearls; the gold and kingfisher-feather work was finely intricate. One look was enough to tell her this was the kind of magnificent object only the palace could produce.

She rarely wore elaborate headdresses — only for formal occasions. She had plenty of jewelry already, and at this moment did not particularly want or not want it.

Still, she nodded. "I like them."

Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan's emotional state, and felt unsettled.

He gestured again. Another attendant came forward, presenting a pair of gold filigree peony hairpins set with gemstones. He held them up before Xi Rongyan's eyes, his dark gaze fixed on her. "And these? Do you like them?"

He thought women always loved such things.

Yet there had been a scene like this in the previous life as well.

She had been wan and listless, not deigning to look even once at the things he gave her.

Wei Qi pressed his lips together, watching Xi Rongyan's reaction without betraying anything.

He did not know how to say the things that pleased women. He had gone to the barren, bitter north while still young — unlike his two elder brothers, who had stayed in the capital and had the leisure to learn the arts of romance.

He only thought: this flower pattern suits her.

In the previous life, Xi Rongyan had refused all his overtures. Because she hated him.

Now at least she no longer hated him.

In truth, one could not deny that the pair of hairpins in the Emperor's hand were delicately and beautifully made. They would look striking and regal worn in the hair.

Xi Rongyan glanced up to meet the Emperor's downward gaze — deep and dark, tender, with more than a trace of feeling.

She could not help wondering: had the Emperor looked at Wang Xiuyi in this same way before?

Of course she knew it was not worth thinking about. This was how the inner palace was — her mother had said the same was true even in ordinary noble households.

She only found herself reflecting: when one was fond of someone, did one really forget so quickly?

Xi Rongyan gave a docile nod. "This concubine likes them."

Her voice was soft as the call of an oriole, yet Wei Qi could tell she did not seem particularly pleased.

He pressed his lips together. His expression was veiled.

He gently slid the hairpin into the dark hair at her temple. Her hair held only the wide, plain white jade pin she always wore. All her jewelry was jade pieces. The ornate gold pin looked somewhat out of place.

Wei Qi's eyes darkened a shade. He only wanted to give her the best of everything he could offer. Perhaps it had never been what she wanted.

His heart stumbled for just that one moment — then he swiftly swept the brief flicker of disappointment aside.

From the moment he had decided to take her from the Gu family, he had stopped caring whether it was what she wanted.

He called the remaining attendants forward and had them display all the jewelry from the trays before her. He looked at her face. "I'll have all of this sent to your palace."

Xi Rongyan was momentarily at a loss — she had not expected the Emperor to suddenly shower her with so many gifts. She quickly moved to rise and offer thanks.

Wei Qi did not let Xi Rongyan rise from his lap. He pressed her back against him, dismissed everyone from the inner chamber, and reached for a dish of rose milk pastries at his side. He picked one up and held it to Xi Rongyan's lips.

His deep, fathomless gaze looked at her. "Try one."

Wei Qi remembered the days he had locked Xi Rongyan in the palace because she kept trying to escape — how she had refused to eat anything. He had threatened her with her child, and only then would she eat a little.

He had used endless strategies, arranging food made to her preferences.

Among all the pastries, the only ones he had seen Xi Rongyan eat more than a few bites of were the rose pastries. He had filed that away.

The milk pastry's particular creamy scent blended with the rich fragrance of rose, and it did genuinely make Xi Rongyan a little tempted.

She had loved pastries since childhood, and milk pastries especially.

With the Emperor's eyes fixed steadily on her, and the Emperor feeding her with his own hand — she was not quite accustomed to it, but she parted her lips all the same and took a small bite.

Seeing Xi Rongyan bite into it, Wei Qi finally smiled. He asked: "Is it good?"

Xi Rongyan nodded.

It was genuinely good — it melted the moment it touched the tongue, not overly sweet, very much to her taste.

She looked at the large remaining piece still in the Emperor's fingertips and reached out her hand. "This concubine will take it."

Wei Qi still held the rest toward her lips, the gesture carrying just enough firmness that refusal would have been awkward. He looked at her. "If you like it, I'll have some sent to your palace every day going forward."

Xi Rongyan looked at the milk pastry being held in front of her again, felt a tiny struggle in her heart, and bit into it anyway.

She hoped they could get through it quickly. Sitting on the Emperor's lap, this close to him, had always made her nervous.

But when she finished, the Emperor reached for another piece. She hastily shook her head. "I cannot eat any more."

Wei Qi raised an eyebrow. "Not even one more piece?"

He still held the rose pastry toward her lips, watching the soft fullness of those lips with a trace of something left dusting them. His gaze grew deep. "Just one more bite, then."

Seeing the Emperor so insistent about holding it out to her, Xi Rongyan had no choice but to take another bite.

The remainder she could only watch as the Emperor put into his own mouth.

Her face grew hot again.

chapters.title: I Have a Hidden Ailment
chapters.content:
The chamber was dim, a thread of daylight falling on that pale, graceful profile.

Wei Qi looked down. He could see the near-translucent fairness of her skin, each fine down hair visible with perfect clarity.

He also noticed her fingers, fidgeting anxiously at the handle of her fan — the nails free of the bold-colored lacquer the other consorts wore, clean and rounded.

From beneath the wide sleeve, a slender wrist appeared, adorned with a faintly purple translucent bracelet, making the skin of that wrist appear even more snow-white by contrast. He rested his palm over the back of her hand.

He stroked for a long while, savoring the smooth and delicate sensation. He closed his fingers around hers, threading them together.

The person in his arms shifted with a trace of unease. Her fragrance drifted up around them, jewels and jade catching the light.

Wei Qi kept his expression calm.

Watching Xi Rongyan still looking somewhat ill at ease, he shifted his posture, leaning down to look into her eyes. Those eyes — they had barely glanced in his direction at all.

Quiet and still. It left Wei Qi mildly dissatisfied.

He was silent for a long while, then tightened his grip on her fingertips and suddenly said: "I have a hidden ailment."

Xi Rongyan had been sitting there wondering why the Emperor had been holding her so long without saying a word. Then she heard this, and looked up in surprise.

The Emperor said he had a hidden ailment?

Why was he telling her this right now? What was his reason?

Xi Rongyan did not know whether to ask further. She opened her lips, looked at the Emperor gazing down at her, and thought — perhaps the Emperor wanted her to ask?

Fortunately, she did not have to deliberate long. The Emperor spoke first.

"My knee was injured some time ago. It aches occasionally. That is why I have been going to Wang Xiuyi's quarters once a month."

"She knows massage, and it provides some relief."

Wei Qi glanced at Xi Rongyan's face. "Now I will no longer be going there."

Xi Rongyan was briefly at a loss — it took her a moment to understand why the Emperor was saying this.

She asked hesitantly: "Why will Your Majesty no longer go?"

Wei Qi looked at her again. "The imperial physician has already treated it."

Xi Rongyan was surprised.

She looked at the Emperor. His meaning was that his visits to Wang Bao'ran had only been for the massage on his knee, and now that it was healed he would go no more?

Why had the Emperor made a point of telling her this?

Besides, the inner palace said the Emperor had favored Wang Bao'ran for a long time. Even if it had only been for his injury, after so long, was there truly not the slightest feeling — that he could simply stop going like that?

Perhaps that was also why people said the Emperor was cold-hearted.

She thought of Wang Bao'ran weeping so brokenly before her today.

Perhaps she too had once believed the Emperor's feelings for her were different.

But in the Emperor's eyes, it had never been that.

No wonder both her aunt and her mother had said: the Emperor's favor was like a burst of fireworks — bright and gone. In the inner palace, one woman's rise was another's fall. No one could be the truly special one.

One must never harbor such thoughts.

Otherwise, in the inner palace it would be nothing but endless, prolonged anguish.

Fortunately, Xi Rongyan truly did not feel the least bit sad about it. She had never considered herself to be the special one.

She paused and then gave a slight nod. Her gaze dropped to the Emperor's fingers around hers, and for a moment she could not think of what to say.

Many thoughts ran through her mind, all the warnings from her aunt echoing at her ear.

Keeping her clearly aware of her own position.

Wei Qi watched Xi Rongyan quietly. His explanation had apparently not produced any happiness on her face.

He felt the old anxiety from the previous life resurface in him.

Without warning he stood, lifting her in his arms. The movement was abrupt enough that Xi Rongyan flinched — her fingers instinctively clutching at his lapels. She realized she was being carried sideways.

She asked in bewilderment: "Where is Your Majesty taking this concubine?"

Wei Qi looked down into those eyes, and without answering her for the first time, carried her in silence toward the inner sleeping quarters.

He set her on his own bed and pressed down over her.

It was still light outside, the day not yet darkened. Xi Rongyan felt her heart race. She saw the Emperor's dark eyes locked on her, and thought — surely he did not mean to, at this hour...

In truth, she had already braced herself. If the Emperor truly intended to, right now — so be it.

It would happen sooner or later, regardless.

Wei Qi truly wanted to.

Just as in the previous life — whenever he was frustrated by her in some way he could not define, he would want her body.

The more she resisted, the more he wanted her.

Right now Wei Qi felt a small setback in his heart. He did not want Xi Rongyan to misread his relationship with Wang Xiuyi — but his explanation did not seem to have made much difference.

The movement when he had laid her down on the bed had not been particularly gentle. The gold hairpin he had put in her hair had slid free onto the pillow, and the wide jade pin sat loosely in her dark hair.

Her white jade eardrops had fallen into her tresses. The fragrance on her person offered constant temptation.

In his heart there was a beast. When it came to Xi Rongyan, though he kept it well-caged, there were always moments when it threatened to break free.

Before his eyes the image kept overlapping — her current face, bright and tender and shy — and her face from the past, pale and swimming in tears.

And then it fixed on that snowy day: her body going soft in his arms as she coughed up blood.

Wei Qi's eyes grew slowly red. His grip on Xi Rongyan's wrists tightened and tightened.

Xi Rongyan watched in horror as the Emperor's eyes grew increasingly terrifying — the look in them as dark and menacing as though he were about to kill.

The pain at her wrists was growing. She cried out in a small, frightened voice: "Your Majesty."

Soft, barely a sound, yet carrying a faint tremor. Wei Qi's gaze locked on Xi Rongyan's panicked face.

He saw himself in that moment reflected in those wide, dark eyes — and no matter how well he hid it, whatever lived in his depths was that same frightening, twisted thing.

Wei Qi drew a slow, deep breath and closed his eyes.

He gathered her back onto his lap and looked down at the wrist he had just gripped. Her fair skin now bore red marks where his fingers had been.

He paused. Tenderness flooded his eyes. He bent and pressed his lips to the marks, then looked at Xi Rongyan with remorse written across his face. "I'm sorry."

Xi Rongyan looked at Wei Qi, still frightened.

It had not been her imagination.

In that moment, the Emperor had been truly terrifying.

She gave a blank nod. The wrist Wei Qi had held — it was still faintly trembling.

Xi Rongyan's frightened, fearful eyes still stung Wei Qi.

He bent and held her tightly, the silence speaking for all the pain in the deepest place of his memory.

He knew there would be a new beginning between him and Xi Rongyan. Yet he could not control himself — could not stop himself from revisiting those fragments of their past together.

Above all, the moment she had quietly gone still and soft in his arms.

It was the one time she had stayed obediently in his embrace.

He had known, then, how deep her grief was.

And he had been utterly powerless.
